title: Insurers' Shifting Priorities - Pricing Modernization Webinar Clip
transcription: Okay, so this data comes from our annual survey of insurers on the factors that shape their IT investment priorities. So last year, and in most prior years, the number one thing is growth. If it'll help me grow, I will spend money. But this year, the picture changed noticeably. Growth, as you can see, moved down to third place, while data and innovation emerged as the leading priorities. In fact, last year, data wasn't even in the top five, and so here it is, number one, without even being something that we saw last year. Now, that does not mean that growth and efficiency are no longer important, because nearly all insurers, 98%, still said growth was a big area of focus in 2026. But what's changing is how they're thinking about achieving it, right? Increasingly, insurers are seeing data as the foundation for growth, innovation, and operational improvement. And so these priorities, they're no longer really separate initiatives, they're deeply interconnected, they're increasingly dependent upon each other. So, growth, number one thing that carriers are focusing on. But at the same time, the market environment is changing. Now, this comes from a study of policyholders who had a personal auto claim in the last two years. And we picked personal auto because we were looking at the claims experience. title: Why Are Top Economists Warning of a Rising Recession Risk in 2026?
transcription: Recession risk is rising fast and could hit within weeks. Will geopolitical tensions and inflation push the global economy over the edge right now? Energy prices are not just a headline. When energy costs rise, businesses face higher expenses and often pass those on to consumers. This causes people to cut back on spending, creating a feedback loop that weakens economic growth. This dynamic is a key reason economists are so worried about inflation's lingering impact on the economy in 2026. Top economist Mohamed El-Erian has issued a stark warning. He says the global economy faces a critical eight-week window to prevent a recession. The trigger is the reopening of a crucial oil route currently disrupted by geopolitical tensions. If this route stays closed, energy supplies tighten further, pushing costs higher and escalating recession risks worldwide. Another leading economist, Mark Zandi, agrees recession risks are rising significantly. He estimates about a 40% chance of recession this year. However, Zandi still sees a path to avoid it, especially if geopolitical tensions ease. The key challenge is managing inflation, which remains elevated even if tensions cool. Investors are already feeling the pressure. Zandi warns the S&P 500 could fall by as much as 30% as the market adjusts to the real economic risks behind inflated stock valuations. This signals a painful correction ahead for many portfolios as the economy deals with these pressures. Even if geopolitical tensions ease and energy routes reopen, elevated prices are expected to persist. Zandi estimates this will cost the average household roughly $1,400 a year. This ongoing inflation squeeze means families will feel the impact directly through higher everyday expenses. What this means for you is clear: the next two months are critical. Energy prices and geopolitical events could shape your financial future. You might face higher costs and a volatile stock market. Staying informed and cautious with spending and investments is key. Subscribe now for the latest updates to help you navigate these uncertain times.

title: Introducing Claude Fable 5
transcription: Today we're launching Claude Fable 5. The most capable model we've ever released to the public. Fable 5 is a mythos class model with safeguards that make it ready for general use. We didn't broadly release our previous model with this level of capability because when we finished training and testing it, we saw that the model, Claude Mythos Preview, was finding thousands of cybersecurity vulnerabilities. A model that can find flaws like that can also be used to exploit them. So instead of releasing it, we handed it to the people who protect the world's critical software and put it to work fixing the holes before someone could break through them. It was the right call for the moment, but it was never the goal. We believe powerful AI should be safe and accessible. That's why we went to work on Claude Fable 5. Every Claude model has safeguards to keep it from doing harm. Fable needed more cautious ones than anything we've built before. Our safety systems for Fable 5 automatically review requests that touch on high-risk areas like cybersecurity or biology. Those requests are then redirected to Opus 4.8. We do that intentionally so people can continue to benefit from the capabilities of a powerful model like Fable without the cyber and biology risks that come with it. The safeguards are broad today, but we'll keep refining them so that they're better at allowing safe requests. We built Claude Fable 5 for your most ambitious work. It can stay with a problem far longer than any model before it. It's highly autonomous and can operate for days without intervention. And it's not just coding. It can take on projects in finance, research, economics, law - complicated tasks that used to need constant supervision. So point it at something that matters. What's the problem we'll look back on and wonder why it took so long to solve? We know what Claude Fable 5 can do. The interesting part is what you'll do with it.

title: Company Culture | Simon Sinek
transcription: So, I think the concept of leadership is one of the most misunderstood concepts in business, quite frankly. We think about leadership as a rank or position, like "I'm in leadership." The question is, are you a leader? Leadership is the awesome responsibility to see those around us rise. It is a skill set that needs to be learned and practiced. Most of us, the way we have achieved our leadership position or rank is because we were good at the job. The problem is that's not your job anymore. You know, when we're super junior, the organizations we work for give us tons of training how to do our job. Some of us go to college and how to do our job. If you're an architect, you have to go to school to learn how to be an architect. And if you're really good at your job, they'll promote you until you reach a position where you're now responsible for the people who do the job you used to do. But they don't teach us how to do that. And so the reason we get managers and not leaders is because we don't get taught how to do our new job called leadership. When leaders take themselves on, when leaders uh become students of leadership, you'll find that all of the traditional metrics that we try and push and, you know, and drive every day, go up. Productivity goes up. Engagement goes up. Uh uh innovation goes up. Um I think it's very funny, I love uh I love organizations that when they write their values on the wall, you know, it's like, integrity, innovation, you know, honesty. By the way, if you have to write honesty on the wall, you've got bigger problems. Um But those those things are not things you can do. Those are the result of things. You can't walk into someone's office and say, "Lynn, a little more a little more innovation from you today, please." Like, what are you supposed to do? And so, it's not a value. A value is is is a behavior. And the better we understand our values and the better we incentivize to behavior, the stronger your culture. And the stronger your culture, the more innovation you get, the more integrity get, the more productivity you get, the more uh uh engagement you get. My favorite definition of culture is culture equals values plus behavior. So, values, number one, needs to be written as verbs. It's not integrity, it's do the right thing. It's not innovation, it's find a new way to solve a problem. It's not honesty, it's tell the truth. Which are which are behaviors and we can incentivize and reward to those behaviors. And the people who are best at embodying those values, those are the ones that we should promote into leadership positions because those are the ones that set the example of of how we how we work here.
caption: In a clear, engaging tone, a man discusses the concept of leadership, emphasizing that it is a responsibility to help others succeed rather than just a rank. He explains that people are often promoted because they excel at their tasks, but they aren't taught how to lead. This lack of training results in managers instead of leaders. When leaders focus on learning, productivity and engagement improve. He concludes that culture is the sum of values and behaviors, and that values should be expressed as actions (verbs) rather than nouns to encourage better leadership.

title: UKREiiF 2026: 'Where the smart money is moving' panel discussion
transcription: So, we're here at UKREIIF this year, talking all things living UK real estate. The current environment for living real estate in the UK is one with viability challenges and concerns. We've got rising build cost inflation, increased regulation, economic difficulties. What there also is, is a huge amount of opportunity. There is pent-up demand, there is under supply, there is no shortage of debt available, there is capital being deployed. It is a huge time for opportunity. The smart money is moving primarily into affordable housing, I would say, though how you define that depends on a number of factors, but clearly the biggest risk to any investment strategy is take-up and demand at this moment, and so through various lenses people are trying to make sure that whatever it is that they're investing in or developing is affordable for the end user, so that the project is viable long-term. I think there's quite a lot of opportunity for living product, because there is a fundamental requirement and demand for good quality accommodation across all the living sectors, asset classes. Especially when there is a bit of an affordability gap. So, those that can deliver product that meets that demand are going to be very well placed. 2026, for me, has also been the year of co-living. We're seeing more institutionalisation of co-living, in terms of an accepted asset class for co-investors. So, I think the opportunities at the moment, very much from a housebuilders point of view, are in the land market. Slightly longer-term strategic sites, gray belt, something where you can work with a landowner to really maximize the number of homes on a site, and really go out there and get a planning consent. I believe that the opportunities in the living sector lie in working in partnership, both with local governments, local councils, with developers, with capital, trying to bring everybody together to achieve the ultimate goal of delivering more housing for the country. I think the smart money in living is moving to affordable with a small 'a'. That's how we deal with the viability concerns. That's where some degree of public subsidy can unlock delivery. I also see there's huge opportunities in partnerships becoming platforms, with long-term sustainable partnerships between registered providers, developers and investors to unlock delivery at scale.

title: Designing the Safer Transit Bus | Innovation for Operator Health
transcription: As was mentioned, I'm Jonathan Hack. I've spent my career in the transportation sector, all in the innovation area. And we've got an exciting panel discussion for you here today. You're going to hear from various perspectives. You're going to hear from the TTC, from Dr. Sarah Fox. You're going to hear from the Amalgamated Transit Workers Union, and you're going to hear from the operators themselves. What I want to talk about today is, um, a kind of deceptively simple idea, which is that if we want safer transit systems, we need to design them with the people who actually do the work. At the end of the day, like, we really want to democratize innovation. We want to make sure that it's cascaded across, so it should be coming from the workers, from the front line. With every new technology that finds its way into the bus, we then take a step back and say, well, how does that now combine with all the other things? Participation is not optional. It's a safety requirement. There's often a tendency to frame innovation that's something that happens to workers. Um, but what this research shows is that transit operators are already experts in safety-critical system management. The challenge moving forward is building processes that recognize and incorporate that expertise.

transcription: Welcome to the Cigna Broker Insight Conference 2026. We are really grateful to have you here. Thank you for joining us. It's great to see so many, uh, familiar faces, uh, here with us. Delighted to have you here to host for what we hope is an engaging, insightful, and enjoyable conversation. Since the opening of our expanded office in May, many of you and your teams have been in with us, have spent time with us through workshops and different working sessions. Our commitment here is long-term, deliberate, and strategic, and Kenya sits right at the heart of that journey. As advocates for improving health, we've been conducting annual insight studies that help us better understand the key aspects of people's health and well-being in order to improve the vitality of those we serve. The data that I will present today reflects a sample of over 500 people in Kenya and over 11,000 globally, and those are not necessarily Cigna customers, but are really a cross-section of of the society. I'm sure you, you will agree with me, because both health and vitality are foundational for thriving individuals, for thriving families, thriving communities, and they help foster, ultimately, a healthy economy, a healthy workforce, and a healthy society. The true value of any health solution is only ever revealed in a moment of crisis. And in that moment, what people desperately need is not just coverage. They need to know that someone is there, someone who knows their name, someone who picks up the phone, and someone who comes to them. Cigna Africa is that someone. We pass our love back to your teams in the offices, please pass our love to them, and we look forward to partnering. Thank you very much. I have been honored to be your MC tonight, and we look forward to seeing more of you in the coming events. Asanteni sana.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 explained: How the new 48-team format works
transcription: For years, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has talked about getting more countries involved at a World Cup. That push finally took shape in January 2017 when football's governing body voted to expand the tournament from 32 to 48 teams. Under the new format, there will be 104 matches at this World Cup. That's 40 more than at Qatar 2022. Those games will be played across 16 host cities in the USA, Mexico, and Canada. That's a huge change from the compact 2022 tournament in Qatar where a fan could realistically attend two or even three matches in a single day. The 48 teams will be split into 12 groups of four. The top two from each group plus the eight best third-placed teams will move into a new 32-team knockout phase. From there, the tournament runs through the round of 32, the round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals, and then the final. By the time we get to the decider at MetLife Stadium in New York, New Jersey, on July the 19th, the champions will have played eight matches. That's one more than the seven required by Argentina when they won Qatar 2022.

title: The 2026 FIFA World Cup explained in 2 minutes
transcription: The stage is set for this year's FIFA Men's World Cup, with the opening matches kicking off tomorrow. The tournament, held every four years, will be unlike any before it. Here's why. Firstly, it will be the biggest World Cup in history, the most complex one yet. For the first time ever, the tournament will be shared across three countries: the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and matches will be played across 16 cities. The competition is expanding, too. Instead of the traditional eight groups, this year's tournament will feature 12, made up of four teams each. 48 national teams will compete, instead of 32. With more teams in the mix, the road to glory could be tougher to predict. The expansion means a record number of matches. Teams will play 104 matches over 39 days, making it the longest ever World Cup run. With more teams involved, there could be more opportunities for underdogs to make their mark. Among those returning to the World Cup include the Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti, and Iraq, while four debutants are getting their boots on the pitch for the first time. They are Uzbekistan, Jordan, Curacao, and Cape Verde. But staging the World Cup across three countries brings major logistical challenges. Some teams could end up traveling thousands of kilometers between venues, crossing borders and time zones. FIFA has grouped matches regionally to reduce travel, but long journeys may still be unavoidable for teams that progress deep into the tournament. And depending on where they're playing, the climates could be different, from the high altitude of Mexico City to Miami's heat and humidity. To manage that, FIFA has mandated cooling and hydration breaks during matches. Next, technology will play a bigger role than ever before. Every player will have a digital avatar to remodel on-pitch actions. These changes make it easier for officials to see what would go on during fast or obstructed plays, so they can provide more accurate calls for offsides or potential handballs. And then, of course, there are the stars. This could be the last dance for several legends. Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed this will be his last World Cup. Argentina's Lionel Messi and Croatia's Luka Modrić are also widely expected to be making their final appearances on the game's biggest stage. For football's greats, one final bow. For a new generation, a chance to make history. The road to World Cup glory is about to begin.

title: How Mohammad Irfan Went From Street Hawker To India's Most Viral Protest Voice
transcription: सिर्फ पेट रोटी खा लेना ही जीवन नहीं है। शहरी सलम में जीवन नरक है। मैं कहता हूँ लोकतंत्र में ना अहंकार नहीं संवाद होना चाहिए और संवाद के दरवाज़े दोनों तरफ़ से खुले होने चाहिए। संविधान की शपथ में ना गरिमा शब्द का, व्यक्ति की गरिमा, राष्ट्र की एकता और अखंडता को सुनिश्चित, तो व्यक्ति की गरिमा, गरिमा, गरिमा नहीं गिरनी चाहिए सर। जय श्री कृष्णा सर, मैं इरफ़ान सर और आज मुझे आपसे बहुत सारी बातें करनी है सर। चार ट्रिलियन की अर्थव्यवस्था में ना पढ़े-लिखों का ही जीवन संवरा है? A voice that rose about the slogans at Jantar Mantar is now being heard in the country's political corridors. Mohammad Irfan, the hawker with little formal education whose speeches went viral during the student protest, met Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday. Rahul Gandhi said Irfan's understanding of the constitution and his desire to learn reflected the strength of India's youth. Hours after the meet, Irfan spoke exclusively to India Today's sister platform, The Lallantop, with a message that cuts across party lines. मैं आज राहुल गांधी से मिला तो मैंने उनसे यही कहा कि अगर सर आप जो हम आपसे अपनी मांगे रख रहे हैं, आप विपक्ष के बड़े नेता हैं और आज नहीं तो कल सत्ता में आएंगे, अगर आपने हमारी बातों के वादाखिलाफी की तो हम अपनी असहमति आपके खिलाफ भी रखेंगे। For Irfan, accountability does not stop with one government or one political party. और हम न्यूट्रल हैं, हम इस देश का भला चाहते हैं। He also spoke about the struggles of migrant workers. 2024 का एनसीआरबी का डाटा कहता है कि 1 लाख 70 हजार 746 मौतें हुई जिसमें 31% दिहाड़ी मजदूर थे और वजह एक थी कि घर में तंगी और मानसिक संतुलन डिस्टर्ब होना, आर्थिक तंगी थी। तो हम कैसे इग्नोर कर सकते हैं उस वर्ग को जो इस देश की बड़ी आबादी है और खून-पसीना लगा रही है इस देश के निर्माण में? हम कैसे इग्नोर कर सकते हैं उसे? From the streets of Jantar Mantar to the national spotlight, his story is not about political power. It's about the power of a citizen's voice to be heard. If you liked the video, do like, comment, share, and subscribe.
caption:
The audio begins with a passionate and energetic speech in Hindi by a man named Mohammad Irfan. His voice is intense, slightly raspy, and filled with conviction as he talks about the hardships of slum life, the true meaning of democracy, and the dignity of individuals. A dramatic, suspenseful instrumental track plays in the background, amplifying his emotional delivery. 

This is followed by a brief, casual clip where Irfan warmly greets someone, saying "Jai Shree Krishna," amidst outdoor ambient sounds and footsteps. 

Soon, a professional male narrator with a clear Indian English accent takes over, introducing Irfan as a hawker with limited formal education whose speeches went viral. The narrator explains Irfan's recent meeting with Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. The background transitions to a motivational, upbeat news-style instrumental track.

The audio continues with a mix of the narrator's commentary and snippets of Irfan's speeches. Irfan speaks with great fervor about political accountability, emphasizing that his dissent will remain even if the opposition comes to power. He also highlights the struggles of migrant workers, citing grim statistics about their deaths and mental stress due to financial hardship. 

The video wraps up with the narrator emphasizing the power of a citizen's voice, followed by an upbeat outro track encouraging viewers to like, comment, share, and subscribe.

transcription: हेलो दोस्तों, हमारे रोहित चंदेल सर के केस को लेकर जितने भी फैंस हैं, आज सुबह से ही हर किसी के मन में बस एक ही सवाल घूम रहा है। क्या आज हियरिंग हुई? क्या कोर्ट से बेल मिली? या क्या रोहित सर को लेकर कोई नया अपडेट आया है? हम सभी फैंस बहुत बेसब्री से इंतजार कर रहे हैं और आप सभी के लगातार आ रहे मैसेजेस और कमेंट्स देखकर मैं अच्छी तरह समझ सकती हूँ कि आप सब भी मेरी तरह कितने परेशान हैं। इसीलिए आज का पूरा सच आपके सामने रखना बहुत जरूरी था। तो बिना किसी एक्स्ट्रा बहस के, सीधे और साफ शब्दों में बता दूँ, आज बेल हियरिंग को लेकर ऑफिशियली कोई भी नया अपडेट नहीं आया है। कोर्ट या लीगल टीम की तरफ से अगली हियरिंग की कोई भी फिक्स डेट ऑफिशियली अनाउंस नहीं की गई है, लेकिन मैं पिछले कुछ दिनों से देख रही हूँ कि सोशल मीडिया और यूट्यूब पर काफी लोग खुद से ही हियरिंग की डेट्स तय कर रहे हैं। हर रोज अपने मन से एक नई डेट बनाकर वीडियो डाल देते हैं कि आज हियरिंग होने वाली है, कल फैसला आ जाएगा या आज बेल मिल जाएगी। लेकिन सच ये है कि ऐसा कुछ भी नहीं है। इस केस से रिलेटेड ज्यादातर लीगल इंफॉर्मेशन पब्लिक नहीं है। कोर्ट का काम अपने हिसाब से चलता है, किसी के अंदाजा लगाने से तारीखें तय नहीं होतीं। इसलिए हर किसी फेक न्यूज़ पर आँख बंद करके भरोसा मत कीजिए। यह सब सिर्फ व्यूज पाने के लिए बनाया जा रहा है। हम सब फैंस रोहित सर का बहुत इंतजार कर रहे हैं और उनके लिए लगातार प्रार्थना कर रहे हैं। हम सब चाहते हैं कि उन्हें जल्द से जल्द बेल मिले और सब सही हो जाए, लेकिन इस इंतजार में हमें स्ट्रांग और पॉजिटिव रहना है। झूठी अफवाहों और फेक वीडियोस को देखकर खुद को परेशान मत कीजिए। पॉजिटिव रहिए और उन्हें सपोर्ट करते रहिए। जैसे ही कोर्ट या लीगल टीम की तरफ से कोई भी असली अपडेट आएगा, मैं सबसे पहले आपके साथ शेयर कर दूँगी। तब तक के लिए अफवाहों पर ध्यान मत दीजिए, पॉजिटिव रहें और चैनल को सब्सक्राइब कर लें ताकि आपको हमेशा सही और सच्ची जानकारी ही मिले। धन्यवाद।

ने 199 रन चार विकेट पर केवल 17.5 ओवर में ही स्कोर कर लिया था। अभी विदेशी खिलाड़ियों ने टीमों को ज्वाइन नहीं किया है, केवल इंडियन प्लेयर इस मुकाबले का भाग हैं। इसके साथ ही रघु शर्मा ने तीन विकेट लिए मुकाबले की कंप्लीट हाईलाइट हमने टेलीग्राम पर डाल दी है और भी बाकी टीमों के जो प्रैक्टिस चल रही है वो सब कुछ टेलीग्राम पर हम प्रोवाइड कर रहे हैं तो आप फटाफट टेलीग्राम चैनल को ज्वाइन कर लें और आप कमेंट And in the end phir Rinku Singh aaye jinhone 40 runs score kiye in just 25 balls aur unki baari mein do chakke bhi shamil the. Umran Malik the samne aur Navdeep Saini jo ke officially announce ho jayenge maybe lagta hai humein as replacement for Harshit Rana, unke samne is Raghuvanshi young up-coming talent ne bahut acha perform kiya. title: Marco Rubio Rails Against 'Globalist Bureaucrats' At ICC And 'So-Called International Law'
transcription: For 250 years, Americans have governed ourselves as a free and sovereign people. We choose our own leaders, we determine our own laws, and when we're accused of a crime, we stand for judgment before a jury of our own peers. This is the essential and indispensable feature of our form of government. It is the foundation of our shared way of life. But today, powerful people in faraway places want to take that away from us. They believe that they should be in charge of your laws, of your country, your life, and they don't care whether or not you agree. Halfway across the world, there's an institution that calls itself the International Criminal Court. Maybe you've heard of it, maybe you haven't. But chances are you don't know the names of its judges, of its prosecutors, or its president, and you shouldn't have to. But as we speak, the ICC and its friends are waging a war against our country, not with bullets or missiles, but with statutes and compacts and the force of so-called international law. When the ICC was born 24 years ago, they told us that it was merely a narrow backstop, a global court that would step in to prosecute only the gravest offenses, things like genocide and war crimes, and only when a nation's courts were unable to prosecute them on their own. But the truth is, it was something far more radical and extreme. It was a global tribunal staffed by unelected globalist bureaucrats who claim their power is almost unlimited. The danger of this global court has only continued to grow. Today, it threatens every aspect of our political and legal system. Border patrol agents removing violent criminals from our country, American Marines risking their lives to defend our homeland, prosecutors working to dismantle terrorist plots to attack and kill Americans. If we stand idle, all of them would be at the mercy of foreign judges thousands of miles away, facing the constant risk of prosecution and even imprisonment for the so-called crime of defending their own country. The American people never agreed to any of this, and they never will. Read the words of our Declaration of Independence. We fought a revolution against a foreign power transporting us beyond seas to be tried for pretended offenses. Independence is our birthright. We will never let foreign bureaucrats take that away from us. This administration will not sit by as the ICC and its allies seek to threaten our people. If they believe they can deprive us of our sovereignty, we will teach them the full meaning of American resolve.

title: 3 Turpin Kids Speak Out After Years Of Being Abused By Parents
transcription: It's a story that shocked the nation. 13 children held captive in a house of horrors by their parents. They escaped, but three of the siblings now say their nightmare continued. They are the 13 kids who were rescued from their parents in 2018. The house of horrors case broke when 17-year-old Jordan Turpin escaped and called 911. I just ran away from home. Okay. My two little sisters right now, chained up. The kids were rescued after years of abuse at the hands of their Elvis-obsessed parents. Won't you wear my ring? Some had been starved and chained to furniture. The parents both plead guilty to charges of child abuse and torture. They were sentenced to 25 years to life in prison in California, and the children entered the state's foster care system. This is the street where Jordan escaped and called 911. You'd think that after everything they'd suffered, their new lives would be happy and fulfilling, but the children are coming forward to speak for the first time about the abuse they say they experienced again at the hands of their foster parents. I mean, something bad did happen the first night I was there. Didn't know very much, but I did know that that was didn't feel right. It was like a nightmare. Three of the Turpin kids are telling their heart-wrenching stories to Diane Sawyer in "The Turpins: A New House of Horrors." They are Julissa, Joylinda, and James. They would do everything in their power, it seemed like, to try to like break me. Attorney Carly Sanchez is representing some of the Turpin children. Some of my clients were sexually abused, they were physically abused, hit, have their hair pulled out. The emotional abuse that these children endured is horrific. They were told by their foster parents, "I understand why your parents chained you up. I would have done the same thing." One abusive foster parent was convicted of child abuse charges and sentenced to eight years. Now, the Turpin kids are trying to rebuild their lives. Something good needs to come from this. title: Highlights | Quantum USA
transcription: Quantum technologies are vitally important to economic prosperity and to national security. Over the next few years, the demand for quantum-literate professionals is going to outpace the supply, and that's something that, you know, we need an answer for. Post-quantum cryptography and the exercise of migrating towards that is far more complex than anyone really understood. It's far more than just switching algorithms. We need to iterate quickly, fail fast, get back up, build the muscle memory to continue to develop what we can with what we have. There are tremendous assets in the field of quantum technology, and what we need to do is better coordinate those by developing an operational strategy and then executing together. It's important to bring people together to discuss things forthrightly and transparently. We have differing opinions perhaps, but it's important to hear those differing opinions. We're thinking about these technologies in terms of a system, how they interconnect, how they relate to one another. We are also thinking about dual-use capabilities in order to accelerate market adoption. We need to bring in different teams with diverse perspectives because we need experts in quantum, we need experts in industry to build the use cases and create those bridges, and then we need people that know how to create that interconnection layer. Now we're dealing in a multi-domain environment, not only just across networking, security, and compute or cloud, but also across land, air, sea, and space. And so all the stakeholders that will ensure a right business or mission outcome need to be involved because it's not just about quantum as a compute, it's really about how we connect and protect that compute to deliver that mission or business outcome. There is a whole lot to be discovered, and now is the time. Collaboration across domain experts, quantum scientists, software developers, business leaders, research centers, I can keep going on and on. Now is the time to start thinking about that. I really think the biggest points for a quantum strategy right now is taking care of the organizational and human layers of this transition. We have so much untapped workforce full of potential who can help us accelerate the adoption of post-quantum cryptography and the quantum strategy overall. The United States is gaining increasing awareness that we need to do better and be thinking ahead about the dependencies we have in our supply chains, advanced R&D investments that are needed to continue advancing enabling technologies that are providing key components for quantum technologies, also growing our workforce to ensure that we can continue innovating at pace as these technologies come to fruition in the next 3 to 5 years. It's critical to get together the public and private sector: policymakers, standards developers, innovators, scientists, and the folks from the commercial world together to talk about the implications of these technologies, how we roll them out, and how we secure them. There's a lot of work, but it's going to be fun, and I'm excited to be a part of it. So thank you for having me.

title: Women in Leadership Conference 2026 Highlights: A Day of Inspiration ✨
transcription: We are at the Grove Hotel and Resort. It is absolutely phenomenal. I think it's our best Women in Leadership conference yet. It's the sixth annual conference. Every year we think it can't get any better, and every year we have amazing speakers, attendees, sponsors, and it just goes to show that community in Hertfordshire is becoming stronger. Days like today are important in- for many aspects, really. I think, first of all, it's about recognizing, celebrating how far women have come and I think it's sometimes really remember that we need to highlight that, but also just how strong women are together and how good we are at having that resilience and supporting and helping each other. And it does feel like a proper safe space, and an opportunity for everyone to grow, which I think is quite unique in the world at the moment. Leadership, particularly as a woman, is not always straightforward. As CEO, you carry the full picture, the commercial weight, the people decisions, the responsibility when things go right and also when they don't. This year's theme of Give to Gain feels incredibly relevant because when women give, something powerful happens. We don't diminish ourselves; we strengthen each other. Just think about what you could achieve now that we do have these amazing technologies and these amazing communities of women supporting us. My key takeaway from today is hearing about women's journeys, and to see from where they started and where they've got to, and I think it reminds us all what opportunities there are out there for us, and what a celebration today to hear these stories. Come on, girls, the world is our oyster. So, at Mad Science of Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire, our mission is to inspire the next great British scientist. So, it feels kind of special to actually be acknowledged for everything that I do leading a team. I have 100 staff members, and, you know, dedicate my time to being a single mom and a business owner, and it's nice to be recognized for that. There's one message that I'd like to leave you with today, especially in a room full of amazing leaders and women: be yourself unapologetically, because that is enough, and then give to others. So, give opportunities, give trust, give feedback, and give support, and more importantly, give encouragement. Go out there, get your gold medal in whatever it may be in life.

title: 2026 NACo Annual Conference: Day 3 Recap
transcription: Day three of NACo's annual conference challenged county leaders to think bigger. The day was headlined by astronaut Colonel Chris Hadfield, who drew on his experiences commanding the International Space Station to share a simple but powerful message: prepare relentlessly, stay curious, and don't let uncertainty stand in the way of progress. Earlier, the general session celebrated the innovation already happening in counties across America, recognizing more than 1,800 achievement award-winning programs from over 140 counties and state associations. Proof that some of the country's most creative solutions are being developed at the local level. That spirit of innovation carried into the exhibit hall, where main stage presentations and common ground conversations connected county leaders with new technologies, fresh ideas, and peers tackling many of the same challenges back home. From celebrating what's working to exploring what's possible, day three was a reminder that the best ideas don't stay in one county, they spread. As the conference nears its end, the momentum continues, but the conversations and connections made here will last long after everyone heads home.

title: Nvidia GTC 2026 — Biggest Takeaways
transcription: I'm Katie Tarasov, here at Nvidia's annual GTC Developer Conference in San Jose, California, where CNBC will have live coverage throughout the event. I'm on the showroom floor where hundreds of companies are showing off products powered by Nvidia's chips and technologies, including a lot of robotics. 110 robots here, almost every single company in the world, I can't think of one that are building robots, is working with Nvidia. Humanoid robots from companies like Unitree, Booster, and LimX greeted me on the way in today. But the star event was, of course, CEO Jensen Huang's keynote. I just want to remind you, this is a tech conference. Nvidia's graphics processing units, GPUs, have proven absolutely crucial for powering generative AI, making the Silicon Valley giant the first ever to reach a $5 trillion market value last year. But now, agentic AI is shifting compute needs, and Nvidia is shifting strategy to match. It showed off a rack filled only with its central processing units, CPUs, at GTC this week. The more modest host chips usually act in a supporting role for GPUs but have suddenly found themselves in the limelight, creating an industry-wide renaissance as Nvidia says CPUs could be the next bottleneck for AI. Huang unveiled a new Groq language processing unit in his keynote Monday, built on technology acquired with Nvidia's largest purchase to date, $20 billion for Groq's assets in December. The new LPU has a single core, purpose-built for speeding up the GPU. It's expected to ship in the third quarter of 2026 and be integrated into a brand new rack dedicated to housing 256 of the new chips, increasing the token-per-watt performance of Rubin GPUs in the neighboring Vera Rubin rack 35 times. We united, unified two processors of extreme differences: one for high throughput, one for low latency. It still doesn't change the fact that we need a lot of memory. And so, Groq, we're just going to add a whole bunch of Groq chips, which expands the amount of memory it has. He also gave a sneak peek of this: Nvidia's Hyper architecture that will be available in the next Vera Rubin Ultra rack-scale system shipping in 2027. It totally changes the game for rack-scale systems by flipping the compute trays on their side to allow extreme density and much lower latency. Huang also met with reporters for a private Q&A session Tuesday. We've been, um, licensed for many customers in China for H200. That's right. Reconnecting with people, the discussion face-to-face, talking to brilliant minds, and exchanging ideas. That is the real value.

I think this year has been quite special for the 21st EU Spectrum Management Conference here in Brussels. Satellite has become one of the trendy topics, one of the most valuable topics also to discuss. And I think the key takeaway that I get is that we all agree on the objectives and the goals that we have. We want to connect everyone, we want to connect Europe and make Europe relevant again in the digital conversation. And for that, satellite is a key component of the ecosystem.

We need to be prepared for the improvements in EU regulation to foster competitiveness and to promote innovation in Europe. We need to be prepared for the WRC-27 and 31 in order to address the best positions for EU interests and we need to be prepared as well with our open mind to converge on the best approach for Europe.

Two things that these conferences are very good at: one is that they try to put together a neutral panel that encompass all the players, so that we can see the discussion from the various points of view, and the other one is the convening power of Forum Global that they can bring together everybody to discuss openly and not to push any agenda forward, so I'm very happy to participate in this kind of events.

transcription:
Spectrum is a complex issue. Spectrum is a scarce resource. Our spectrum needs should be clearly defined well in advance. This would have a significant impact on people on the ground. We have to accommodate and understand each other. Move towards harmonization collectively.

I think this was a fantastic event, which brought different perspectives, like 5G, 6G, innovation, and the digital divide. This was a, a significant and important step to prepare for WRC-27, because this will have a significant impact on people on the ground, right? So, I think that will help us harmonize, or move towards harmonization collectively.

Yeah, there are three key takeaways: the first one is the contentious WRC-27; the second one is the direct-to-device progress and regulation; and the last one is the spectrum roadmap that is vital for the investment and the digital growth.

I'm very glad that we were able to share the Philippine case, our developments in the country, especially now that we have a new act, the Konektadong Pinoy Act. Of course, we know that spectrum is a scarce resource, so it's important to learn from the industry and other administrations.

We have already a clear roadmap defined, first 6 GHz, 7 GHz, we call it golden band, and our spectrum needs should be clearly defined well in advance.

Spectrum is a complex issue. It involves a wide range of stakeholders with varying viewpoints, and in order to balance those viewpoints and come up with a, a solution, the only way really to get there is to put them all in the same room. If you put everybody in the same room without any structure, um, we have chaos. So, Forum Global bring to that discussion the structure within which we, as representatives of industry, can work out solutions, or work out ways forward.

So, I'd like to thank Forum Global for hosting the 12th APSMC. The timing would have not been better than this, because all the APT countries are actually preparing for the WRC now, and we are preparing to have a good harmonized view for the conference. These will help us to deliver what we are looking forward from 6G use cases like AI or XR and sensing. We need to have a harmonized contiguous band.

As usual, I think Forum Global has done an amazing job. This event is particularly important for the industry, because we have the opportunity to discuss with regulators, and with other members and different sectors. title: RSAC 2026 Conference Quick Look: The Impact of Security Usability Challenges in Cloud Environments
transcription: Hi everyone, my name is Alex Sierra and on behalf of myself and Alex Pinto, my co-presenter, I want to talk to you about a session CLS W09: The Impact of Security Usability Challenges in Cloud Environments. The point of this talk is we're going to be looking at a dataset that involves security posture checks on a variety of cloud providers, especially the hyperscalers: AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure). And we're going to correlate the UX decisions that they have made in the way that users can set up infrastructure, can set up credentials, can set up storage, with security outcomes. We're going to see how much, and if and how much, the way that the cloud providers decided to design their UI and their architecture are leading users to make more or less security mistakes. We feel like this is important for cloud providers and for people designing systems in general to understand the impact of their user experience design in security. Plus, we provide a series of practical recommendations for organizations, for companies, in the way that they use those cloud providers to minimize the impacts that those UX decisions have on their security posture. Hope to see you all there.

title: Kevin Baum - Next Generation in AI Research IJCAI-ECAI 2026
transcription: Hi, I'm Dr. Kevin Baum and I lead the research group for Responsible AI and Machine Ethics at the German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence. Being a philosopher and computer scientist, I work on a problem that sounds simple, but that might be one of the most important ones in our lifetimes. The alignment problem. Put simply, it is about getting AI to do what we want in ways we find acceptable. But that framing actually hides the hard part. We live in a pluralist society and we do not agree on what we want or on what counts as acceptable. So aligning AI with human values is more than a technical challenge, it's a sociotechnical one under deep normative uncertainty. At bottom of it, it's a political problem. Whose values, decided by whom, and why? My group works on that challenge from a philosophical and a computer science point of view. We build architectures that make AI reason explicitly about norms and values, resulting in normatively competent systems that can act for the right reasons, state those reasons, and let human challenge and refine them, and we ground all that in philosophical theory. Here's why it matters. AI systems are becoming agents, making decisions in hospitals, courtrooms, and classrooms. The answer is not smarter machines, it is normatively more competent ones. Doing the right things for the right reasons, guided by real humans and keeping responsibility where it belongs.

transcription: ...and then get the PET scan, get the MRI to rule out other causes. But most importantly, there is a specific test for Lewy body dementia where we actually do a synuclein, um, skin biopsy. So, we take a punch of skin from the back of the neck, and we stain it, and we look at it under a microscope, and we can actually see these alpha-synuclein proteins deposited within the skin. And if we see an elevation of these and a negative DaTscan—which the DaTscan is the diagnostic test for Parkinson's disease—we can now know that we're leaning much more to a, to a Lewy body dementia diagnosis, as opposed to the Parkinsonian features. Um, so again, cholinesterase, the, the memantine, they do help. We have to be careful though because treating Parkinson's when you don't have Parkinson's causes trouble in itself. We try to unfreeze muscles, so putting you on medication that you don't need is, is actually problematic. And again, you've got to avoid the atypical antipsychotics in Lewy body disease. The agitation, the hallucinations we see commonly in Alzheimer's and use medications such as Rexulti or, um, quetiapine, which is Seroquel, is actually contraindicated in Lewy body disease because it will actually make you worse. And then, the non-pharmacological, um, components: support sleep—people who don't sleep are more confused—um, physical, occupational therapy—if you're shuffling, if you're falling, we don't want to add to a problem. So, in summary, um, Alzheimer's disease: hippocampal-predominant neurodegeneration, we can see it on an MRI scan, we have treatments for this. Um, vascular dementia: cerebrovascular, um, injury, strokes—prevent the strokes, prevent dementia. Um, frontotemporal dementia is atrophy within the behavioral and language areas, so instead of looking for memory problems, look for behaviors, look for problems with speech. And then alpha-synuclein pathology within the Lewy body dementia: cognitive fluctuations and very early onset, um, hallucinations—that is, that is sort of the key factor. Um, dementia is not a normal part of aging. We don't have to get more forgetful as we get older. We get slower, it takes longer to recall a fact, it takes longer to, you know, come up with a solution, but dementia is not normal. And then early diagnosis is the cornerstone of treatment. At the moment, we cannot undo the damage that dementia has done. We can't undo the loss of memory. And certainly with the findings that we're seeing now, we've got this 15-year window of this preclinical, um, time. This is where we need to be getting in with the medications. This is where we need to be preventing, you know, worsening of disease in our 40s, 50s, before those symptoms come on in our 60s.

transcription: It is very important to keep routine because if every day you have to wake up and think of doing something new, it takes a lot of energy. Put that down because those repetitive questions, the person with dementia doesn't know they are repeating. What time is my doctor's appointment? 10:00. Ten minutes later, what time is my doctor's appointment? 10:00. That's a frustration for the person caring for the patient with dementia. So, I tell my patients, what time's my doctor's appointment? 10:00. Write it on the board. Next time you're there, what time's my doctor's appointment? Go check your board. So, you know, we we try to keep everything relaxed. And if depression does come on, we can get it treated. title: Nobody Is Really Listening to Your Conference Talk… Here’s Why?
transcription: Big misunderstanding or misconception I find working with scientists, and especially younger professionals, who idealize talking at a conference because a lot of people think that, "Okay, I'm talking to professionals in my field. They already know everything. I only need to show them the best of my data or the best of my method." Well, that's a big misconception. Yes, you're talking to professionals, but in reality, like you said, they are from different part of the brain, or they study different part of rocket science. And they are super tired at that conference, and they have their own agenda at that conference. They are worrying about presenting, or talking to someone, or finding collaborators. Most of them are actually right there on their phones or on their computers while you're presenting. So the reality of that communication is not at all what we romanticized in our head. You know, we romanticized one-on-one, really sitting down to them and talking to that professional who's super interested. title: Beyond Physiology: Dr. Fearon Discusses CathWorks FFRangio's Robust Clinical Evidence
transcription: As you've also heard, uh, coronary physiology continues to be underutilized, and there's probably a number of reasons. It can take extra time, there are issues with the wire-handling characteristics, pressure drift, and other, uh, factors associated with the measurement can be frustrating. If you're measuring FFR, the side effects of adenosine, uh, it's expensive, and there is a small risk anytime you put a wire in a vessel. And as you can see, all of these issues are related to the need for a coronary pressure wire, as well as the use of hyperemic agent like adenosine. And so that raises the question, well, what if we could get all of this information just with the angiogram alone and no need of a pressure wire or adenosine? And that's where angiography-derived, uh, physiology comes into play. Now, six years ago, we published, uh, these data comparing, uh, FFR Angio to wire-based, uh, FFR in a blinded fashion, 10 centers, over 300 patients. And you see that there was a very high, uh, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy, all above 90% with FFR Angio. And, well, what we found even more impressive was if you look at the gray zone or around the cut point of the FFR cutoff of 0.80, this is where most tests have a, uh, accuracy of 50%, kind of like a coin flip. You see that FFR Angio continued to have excellent diagnostic characteristics in that gray-zone area. We also looked at how FFR Angio compares with the non-hyperemic pressure ratios with regard to its correlation with, uh, wire-based FFR. And you see that the accuracy of FFR Angio was actually higher, uh, than the resting indices, uh, when compared with pressure-wire-based FFR. So, what data do we have with FFR Angio? Well, we have a real-world registry looking at the safety of deferring lesions in almost 900 patients, and showing a very low event rate, uh, at one year in those patients where PCI was deferred based on FFR Angio, so reassuring that you can safely defer if you get a negative FFR Angio. And we also now have randomized clinical trial data from Japan. 400 patients in the provisional trial across 13 Japanese sites looking at intermediate lesions. The primary endpoint of this study was non-inferiority of revascularization rate of FFR Angio compared with wire-based FFR. And the investigators met the primary endpoint. Uh, FFR Angio, uh, was non-inferior and had a similar, uh, revascularization rate. They also saw a significantly lower, uh, radiation exposure, 20% reduction with FFR Angio compared with wire-based. And they followed the patients now out to one year, and have shown that major adverse cardiac events, both with and without procedural MI, were, uh, equivalent, if not numerically lower, uh, with the FFR Angio group, so very reassuring data.

The results demonstrate FFR Angio's high sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy, even in the "gray zone" around the 0.80 cutoff. He also references real-world registry data and a randomized clinical trial from Japan (the PROVISION trial) showing the safety of deferring lesions based on FFR Angio, reduced radiation exposure, and favorable one-year clinical outcomes compared to wire-based FFR.

title: PulseCast: Highlights in Leukemias From the 2025 ASH Annual Meeting
transcription: Amir Fathi, a leukemia specialist at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts. I was fortunate to attend the American Society of Hematology meeting this last December in Orlando, Florida, where multiple presentations covering a series of topics in myeloid malignancies were provided. It was an exciting meeting. There were multiple exciting presentations. Among them, we presented the results of PARADIGM, a phase 2 randomized study that compared intensive induction chemotherapy to less intensive azacitidine and venetoclax in fit, traditionally induction-eligible patients. The study met its primary endpoint: event-free survival was better for patients who received azacitidine and venetoclax. There were also multiple secondary endpoints that were important. The rate of overall response, composite remission, was significantly higher in patients who received azacitidine and venetoclax. Patients who received azacitidine and venetoclax also tolerated treatment better, with less incidence, with lower incidence of grade 3 or higher bleeding or infectious complications, decreased time in the hospital, as well as decreased admission during their initial course to the intensive care unit. There was also better quality of life and better patient-reported outcomes. This opens the field to potentially introducing less intensive therapies for patients that are traditionally thought to receive intensive chemotherapy, the long-term standard of care in AML, which allows tolerability, safety, but also allows them to move on to curative modalities such as stem cell transplant. There was also a series of presentations on the combination of azacitidine and venetoclax and targeted therapies, such as gilteritinib, the FLT3 inhibitor, as well as multiple menin inhibitors, such as ziftomenib. These data, although early, show significant promise also in patients with acute myeloid leukemia. I look forward to future meetings and ongoing progress in myeloid malignancies. Thank you.

title: Theo Vincent - Next Generation in AI Research IJCAI-ECAI 2026
transcription: Have you ever wondered if it is possible to reproduce human intelligence inside a computer? Hi everyone, I'm Théo Vincent, a PhD student at the German Research Center for AI, called the DFKI. Recent breakthroughs in generative AI are impressive, but they remain far from human intelligence, mainly because they are limited to imitating human data, and they rely on vast computational resources. My research tackles these challenges by developing algorithms that learn from experience. Learning from experience is the field of reinforcement learning, where a sequence of optimization problems needs to be solved. I proposed algorithms that solve those problems in parallel, thereby speeding up the learning process. This framework is called Iterated Temporal Difference Learning. Regarding resources, a lot of energy is spent tuning hyperparameters of learning agents. I proposed methods that adjust the agent's hyperparameters to its learning pace, thereby eliminating the need to tune hyperparameters and therefore saving resources. I'm excited about future learning algorithms that will learn from experience just as humans do. If you're interested, feel free to check my website.

title: Diary Entry I Wanted To Share With ALL Footballers...
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I wanted to share with you guys a diary entry that I wrote during a time that felt like nothing was going smoothly. And you might want to save this video for later because someday you're going to need it. Recently, I've been questioning why nothing in my life seems to be going smoothly. I've been playing football at a high level for years, training harder than everybody else, taking it more seriously than ever before. And still, I'm sitting here with no confirmed answer about where I'm playing next season. Football is competitive, I understand. I have been trying to get my European visa for the past year. I made three different applications and eventually left the country hopeless. And just two days after leaving, they called me for the acceptance meeting. Just two days after I'm out of the country, probably just bad timing, right? I graduated school with a top 1% mark, went to the best university in my country, signed with a professional club, and made a system so strong it changed the lives of 300 players remotely worldwide. And yet, parents are still skeptical to work with me and delay for months just to say no. Probably just a bad coincidence, right? This might be unrelated, but I even approached a trusted brand of dental braces, and halfway through the treatment, I was the first client in company history who had manufacturing issues, so I had to restart the process. And when they sent me the new one, the package got held at customs, and now I have no idea where the $4,000 worth of dental braces are. Just simple procedures that were initially planned to run smoothly and take a few months to complete are now becoming a headache because it's taking a few years to overcome. This is the side of football, the side of life that nobody ever talks about. Every single year without fail, I go through a season like this, a stretch where nothing seems to click, where it feels like the universe itself has turned against me. And here's the lesson I learned from this and what I wanted to share with you guys today. The toughest battles in life are given to the strongest warriors, not because life is cruel but because life is precise. The moment you decide to achieve something amazing, the moment you decide to become a professional footballer, the universe will place you in difficult situations to see what you're made of, to see whether you'll push through to the other side or whether you'll make excuses, blame the system, and quietly walk away from your dream like most people do. Most footballers quit before the breakout even happens, not because they weren't talented enough but because they stopped one season too early. And here's a harsh truth: for the majority of your life, you're going to be in the fight, you're going to be grinding, uncertain if it's going to work out, waiting for the right moment, pushing through the season when nothing feels fair. And then all of a sudden, for a small percentage of your life, everything is going to start to click. You're going to be playing your best football, your confidence is going to be untouchable, the doors are going to start opening up. And that moment right there, that moment is only beautiful because of everything that came before it. The goal in football or in life is not to avoid the hard season. The goal is to refuse to leave before the season ends. So, if you're in it right now, keep training, keep building, keep showing up every single day for your standards when everything around you feels like it's not. You will only fail the moment you decide to quit, and that's a guarantee. So, do not stop and keep pushing till the end.

title: How to Create a Line of Credit Account in QuickBooks Online (Step-By-Step) [2026 guide]
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to create a line of credit account in QuickBooks Online. Having a line of credit account set up in QuickBooks is essential for tracking borrowed funds and repayments accurately within your financial records. Whether you're managing a small business or keeping personal finances in order, this process will help you stay organized and ensure your books are complete and up to date. If you don't already have a QuickBooks Online account, you can use the link in the description to sign up and get started. Now, let's dive into the steps. First, start by logging into your QuickBooks Online account and navigating to your dashboard. Look to the top right corner of the screen where you'll see a small gear icon. This is your settings menu. Go ahead and click on it to open the options. From the dropdown menu that appears, you'll need to scroll down and select the option labeled "Chart of accounts." This is where all your accounts are managed and organized within QuickBooks. Once you're on the chart of accounts page, look towards the upper right corner of the screen again and click the button labeled "New." This will allow you to create a new account. Next, you'll need to enter a name for the account you're setting up. You can choose something straightforward like "Line of Credit," or use a name that better suits your specific needs. It's helpful to pick a name that makes the account easily recognizable when you're reviewing your records later. After naming the account, it's time to assign the correct account type. In the dropdown menu for account type, select "Long-term Liabilities." This category is appropriate because a line of credit typically represents a financial obligation that spans longer than a year. Once you've set the account type, move to the detail type field. From this list, choose "Notes Payable." This detail type is the most accurate for a line of credit, as it represents loans or borrowings that need to be repaid. Finally, click the "Save" button to complete the process and create your new line of credit account. Once saved, the account will appear in your chart of accounts list, and you'll be able to use it to track transactions related to your line of credit. And that's it! You've successfully created a line of credit account in QuickBooks Online. If you found this video helpful, please like and subscribe.

He begins by explaining why tracking a line of credit is important, then guides the listener through logging into their QuickBooks dashboard, clicking the gear icon for settings, and selecting "Chart of Accounts." title: Video 3: Why is sharing your radiotherapy treatment story important to you?
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: It's been really important to me all along to share my story of my treatment, my diagnosis, my treatment and my recovery, to whoever will listen, to be perfectly honest. My first desire was to tell fellow patients, and I was interviewed by a radiation oncologist. My answers to my, her questions were recorded, and those videos have been shared by doctors and other cancer team members to thousands of people who've been diagnosed with a head and neck cancer. And I'm just so grateful that clinicians have seen the value of sharing a patient's story. I think there's no substitute for a patient who's about to have radiotherapy to hear the story of a fellow patient, not only just describe what the treatment's like and the recovery's like, but just to see a patient who's survived, who's survived cancer. Because I think so many of us when we get that cancer diagnosis, we're just full of anxiety and fear, and there's nothing as reassuring as seeing a patient who's gone through it and come out the other side. But I also think it's good for cancer team members to see these videos because it, it exposes them to the emotional and psychological impact of a cancer diagnosis and the treatment. And if they can hear the patient's story, empathize, uh, understand emotionally, feel some of those feelings, I think they're much more likely to do research and make an effort to help us psychologically, which I think is as important as survival.
caption: In this audio recording, a mature female speaker with a clear Australian accent speaks passionately about the importance of sharing her experience with cancer diagnosis, treatment, and recovery. Her tone is warm, empathetic, and deeply reassuring as she describes her desire to help fellow patients overcome their anxiety and fear by seeing a survivor. She also highlights how sharing these stories can benefit cancer care teams by helping them understand the emotional and psychological impacts of the disease, potentially driving further research in psychological support. A gentle, uplifting instrumental track plays in the background, complementing her hopeful and encouraging message.

I think it's rare that you get to have those experiences, sort of, in the medical field um, to see somebody who has seen you for years, who you see on a regular basis, and really knows, sort of what you need to work on, what you want to work on. So, I really appreciate having a long-term um, partnership, I guess, with the practitioners here in the practice. Um, and, I mean, it's it's a very inviting environment. It's calm, it's really pleasant, everyone who works here is so lovely and helpful. And, those are things that, you know, you don't always find in the medical world, or the, you know, alternative medicine. So, that's been very appealing to me, as well. And, I think that is, is also interesting, and, and, and helpful in healing of all kinds. So, I appreciate that time, sort of, take to myself while this, the acupuncture is actually working on me, and helping solve the issues that I face. Um, yeah, I mean, I would recommend it. I think I just tried it because I'd heard many good things over the years, and read studies about how effective acupuncture could be. And, then coming here and seeing how it's helped, you know, from knee injuries and foot injuries from climbing, to me just having a lot of trouble with insomnia. Like, it's a kind of an amazing thing that it can work in so many different ways. Um, so, it was, I'm glad that I tried it, and I would recommend that other people try it, too. title: I Called My Parents and Said "I Need Help" | Logan's Story
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Before treatment, I was I was broken. I had a lot of depression, anxiety and was using drugs and alcohol to mask all that, to cope with it. I just remember feeling so hopeless. I just broke down and I called my mom and I called my dad and I said, "I need help." I remember at that moment I I still didn't feel great but I felt for the first time that I might be headed in the right direction. In terms of choosing this treatment center, I remember there was a family friend that we had. She said, "If I had a family member going through what Logan's going through, there's only one place I would send them and that was Providence." I think walking around the center and talking to different staff, you know, a lot of the clinicians made me feel like I was understood for the first time in a in almost forever. It was also fun, too. I think that's something I didn't expect is the idea that I can work on myself and I can do the tough things and I can have the groups where I tear up and I can go into individual session and talk about things I haven't talked about but at the same time with all my peers and and even a lot of the staff I was just laughing and I was having a good time. Life now is great. I don't worry people anymore. Soon after graduating Providence, I got hired and I really just started to find my purpose and find my life. The advice I would give someone that's still struggling is stop digging. Find the people in your life who care about you and ask them for help. The answers to the questions that people might have of what happens after treatment, answer themselves when you just give into the experience. So, ask for help. Uh stop digging. I promise you that you're going to be surprised with the outcome.

transcription: Let's talk about anxiety. There was a time where I wasn't just scared of food. I was terrified of it. The fear would build, turn into anxiety, and sometimes end in full panic attacks. My heart would race, my heart would spiral, and at this point, eating felt impossible for me. Even though that I knew that my body needed the food, I just couldn't because of the panic attack. This is something I have been struggle with for a long time. And at this point, I was exhausted, exhausted about living in that constant fear. Fear of food, like, normal people could eat, but why couldn't I? Why was I so scared of it? Starting medication was a big turning point for me. Of course, it didn't turn everything around overnight, but it helped quiet the panic enough for me to actually fight for my recovery. And I think I'm sharing this with you guys because I know how scared and lonely it can feel when food triggers anxiety and panic. And I just want you guys to know that you're not alone and you're not a broken human. So, for those of you who don't know where to start, just ask for the help because there is help out there. And I promise you that it can get better. And if you don't believe me, then I'm a living proof of that.

title: Just a little flower and talk therapy for my fellow moms... #Shorts #lindseybosway
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: My two boys are napping. I have my coffee and I'm going to use just Trader Joe's flowers and make a little arrangement. Let's chat motherhood. After I had my first baby, I think looking back on it, I had more postpartum anxiety than I even knew at the time. And I did not feel like myself for like 15 months. And part of that was just like no creative drive, no desire to really do anything outside of motherhood. And when I had my second, it was definitely better, but I just remember one day he was like 12 months old and I was like, "Oh, I want to make a flower arrangement." And I was like, "Oh gosh, I'm coming back." But it is wild. So, if you're not there yet, if you just had a baby and you feel like you're not yourself, I promise it gets better. And one day you'll feel like doing something again that requires energy. But it's okay if right now you just want to nap when your baby naps. So, I just made a little grid here. That'll make it easier to stick our flowers in. And once I started doing flowers when they were napping, I feel like I have so much more energy on the days that I do it. I think it's just like using your brain for something other than motherhood, and it gives me like a jolt of energy. And often times, when we're dealing with our babies or toddlers, it's such chaos. And I just find arranging flowers to be so peaceful and meditative once you really get into it. I always think about that one creator who talks about getting her pink back. And, you know, it went viral or whatever, but it's so true. And when you're a first time mom, you have no perspective on the fact that it does come back. Your second time around is a little easier because you know what's going on, and you know that it's okay to feel that way. But it can be really jarring when you have your first baby, and you don't understand that it's temporary. It really is. Like my biggest piece of advice that I give friends is just to try to remember in motherhood that everything is temporary. It's looking really pretty, but we have a lot of space to fill in. A few finishing touches here. I also think, in motherhood, it is okay if one day you want to make this huge, amazing arrangement, and the next day you don't want to. You put your kids to bed, and you spend the next hour in your bed. It's just okay. That's how it goes. And you know what I've stopped doing? Bullying myself for that. Just let myself relax. I don't ever go to a space of shame. Because you know what's not relaxing? Sitting down, trying to relax, and worrying about the fact that you're relaxing. Here she is. She's whimsical. She's fall. I love her.

And it's something that I'm picking up on in my continuous healing work, in my own personal um journey, and just growth in general, um for people who do internalize, who could relate to this. So what I'm noticing is, is that sometimes when you internalize, it could happen very subtly. You may not even realize it. And I know I wasn't, per se, and I'll share an example, like, for instance. I had a therapist that they only have a 50-minute session when you sign up with them. And I like this therapist a lot, like I feel like I'm definitely getting work done with them, right? But I noticed that they show up late on the sessions, but they do end on time. That's a thought process, right? And it's internalizing it when I'm not willing to have the conversation with that therapist, even though I think it's something I could deal with, or maybe I think it's small, or maybe I'm trying to observe it a little bit more. To not internalize that looks like having a conversation, even if you don't think that it's a big deal, or maybe you think it is, or maybe it could be a potential problem. Not internalizing that would look like having an actual conversation. And maybe that looks like me saying, "Hey, you know, I notice that our sessions, you do um come in late. You usually start late, but you end on time, and I I feel like I'm not getting the full, you know, time." And I have a few options, right? I could even ask, "Hey, could I expect that you're going to show up late during every session? And if so, if that's something that I could expect, that you normally don't come on the sessions on time, am I going to get my full 50 minutes?" That's a part of what it would look like to not internalizing it. Instead of me just thinking it, allowing it to fester without having a conversation and allowing it to potentially become a problem where I start to feel a way inside instead of having a conversation. All right? So, just just sharing that with y'all. And maybe, you know, you'll find value in that if you are somebody who internalizes.

title: Deepening Self-Awareness: Practical Activities and Reflections #selfgrowth #mentalhealth #selflove
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Self-awareness helps us better understand the thoughts, emotions, and patterns that shape our lives. Here are three simple ways to deepen your self-awareness. Number one, journaling your thoughts. Sometimes clarity begins when you finally see your thoughts on paper. Number two, sitting quietly with your emotions, not avoiding them, not distracting yourself, just noticing them. Number three, asking yourself difficult but honest questions: "What triggers my stress?", "What patterns keep repeating in my life?" At American Behavioral Clinics, we believe self-awareness is one of the most important steps toward emotional wellness and personal growth. Because self-awareness isn't about perfection. It's about noticing, understanding, growing. American Behavioral Clinics, helping people better understand themselves, one step at a time.

title: The Bright Side of AI
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: With all the AI gloom and doom, I often forget how cool AI actually is. Like, what a technology, what a time to be alive. You know, like, I often have this heaviness about it, and more of this, "I gotta use this. I gotta make this work. I need to catch up with with the trends and everything, not to fall behind." And what I lose sight of sometimes is how amazing this technology is, and I just, today, I had this case of, hey, you can, you can use AI to analyze your thought patterns, like your personal thought patterns, and not only can you understand how you think, but obviously also where your blind spots are, and and how you can improve your thinking, and how, what are, what the patterns are, and this, getting this awareness about yourself, in all kinds of areas, obviously professionally, how you make decisions, but but also in private, it's such an amazing feat, to be honest. This technology didn't exist. Like, how would you else, like, get to this? Like, of course, if you do therapy for 10 years, which nobody wants, and and I'm not really a fan of it, still, there's this other person processing it, and you probably not get to the root of it. Now, you can upload hours, hundreds of hours of you interacting in in Zoom calls, whatever it is, and you can have AI analyze, find out your thought patterns, even like making your thoughts visible to yourself. And I just thought, how amazing, and this is just one use case, obviously. There's so much to be had also with this technology. It's scary. It's It puts a pressure on myself, and I guess on you as well, but it's also fabulous, and this is my, my little reminder to myself, and maybe to you, that if you, if you set aside this, this pressure, this, this fear maybe even, and and let in the, the possibilities and the opportunity a little bit more, it could be tremendously fun to interact with this technology, and and all the, the beautiful things that can come from that. See you in the next video.

title: DEPRESSION
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You really fail. Grabe ang nadudulot ng depression sa mga tao ngayon 'no? You think I care about that? Kaya minsan hindi ko maiwasang tanungin ang sarili ko. Don't you care what people think? Doesn't it bother you that people are making you out to be a joke and that I'm being included in that? Ano nga bang pakay ko? Kasi kadalasan gusto ko lahat may aakay sa'kin. Di namamalayan sa mga tanong laging sagot, ano bang malay ko? You want to be really great? Then have the courage to fail big and stick around. Lahat 'to saan papunta? Tangina sa totoo lang hindi ko rin alam kung saan ako pupunta. Babe, that's right. Do you? Nawawalang kamalayan, ayaw maiwan, ayaw ring mauna. Ayaw kong magsimula kasi huli na ang lahat. You're better than that. You really fail. Paano pa ako papalag kung sa utak ko talo na agad? You fail, you fail, you fail, you fail, you fail. Haay. Sa bugtong hininga nalipat ang pahina. Paano pa ako magpapahinga kung 'di ko naramdaman sa bawat paghinga? Now, if you know what you're worth, then go out and get what you're worth. But you gotta be willing to take the hits. Pwede ba akong magreklamo? Saan naman ako magsusumbong? Kanino ko naman ikukuwento ang lungkot na umaalulong? Wala, 'wag na baka matawag pang mahina. Lalo na't 'di pa nakikita mga dapat kong ipakita. Try again. Fail again. Fail better. Let me tell you something you already know. The world ain't all sunshine and rainbows. It's a very mean and nasty place, and I don't care how tough you are, it will beat you to your knees and keep you there permanently if you let it. You, me, or nobody is gonna hit as hard as life. But it ain't about how hard you hit. It's about how hard you can get hit and keep moving forward; how much you can take and keep moving forward. That's how winning is done!
