title: Why We Will Never "Cure" Cancer
transcription: In 1971, Richard Nixon signed the National Cancer Act and declared war on cancer. The language was deliberate: a war with a target date, the way you'd talk about landing on the moon. 55 years later, cancer still kills about 10 million people a year worldwide. We didn't lose that war through lack of funding. The United States alone has poured well over $100 billion into cancer research since that signature. We lost it because the enemy was never a single enemy. That's the part the fundraising campaigns skip. Cancer isn't a disease. It's a category closer to infection than flu. Breast cancer alone splits into at least four molecularly distinct diseases that happen to grow in the same organ. Lung cancer, pancreatic cancer, leukemia: different biology, different mutations, different behavior, filed under one word because they share a symptom: cells that won't stop dividing. Asking for a cure for cancer is a little like asking for a cure for infection. Which infection? Which mechanism? Which host? Point one: The enemy evolves faster than you can aim. Here's the detail oncologists live with and rarely get to explain on camera: a tumor isn't one clone of identical cells. Peter Nowell described this back in 1976 in a paper called "The Clonal Evolution of Tumor Cell Populations," and the idea has only gotten scarier with better sequencing. A single tumor is a population: genetically diverse, competing internally, mutating with every division. Give it a drug, and you're not killing the tumor. You're running a selection experiment. The cells sensitive to the drug die. The handful that happened to carry a resistance mutation before treatment even started now have the whole tumor to themselves, no competition left. Six months later, the cancer comes back, and it comes back immune to the exact drug that shrank it. This is why remission and cure are different words. Oncologists know the difference intimately.

title: Beyond Silos: Transformative Change for the Caribbean
transcription: Across the Caribbean, environmental pressures are no longer unfolding separately. Climate instability, biodiversity decline, rising food dependence and economic vulnerability increasingly collide, amplifying risks across ecosystems, livelihoods and communities. For small island developing states, the consequences are deeply interconnected. So, from food security right through to spiritual well-being, ability to heal and restore, biodiversity plays a critical role. So, this sector needs to go beyond the symptom, the symptoms of the crisis. We have to go deeper. And these are things that I think the environmental sector has avoided for too long. At the second Caribbean regional trialogue, participants repeatedly returned to one central idea, interconnected crises cannot be solved through isolated action. The discussions challenged traditional approaches that treat biodiversity, climate, food systems and development as separate policy areas. What the nexus assessment did is very different from a lot of the previous assessments. It sought to move away from the piecemeal approaches and the siloed sectoral thinking to looking across different sectors: health, food, climate, biodiversity, to find response options that will deliver multiple co-benefits at scale. The conversations also reinforced that these systems extend beyond national borders. As a region, as a Caribbean, it forces us to contemplate how we treat with our neighbors.

title: Scientists Want This Banned | STEM Loft
transcription: Mirror, mirror on the wall. What's the scariest biology concept of them all? Well, there is some scary science out there. One that's getting the attention of biologists right now is called mirror life. Although even the possibility of creating it is still a long way off, scientists are talking about setting guardrails on exploring this area of research now because of the major impact it could have for life on Earth. Just because we can research something doesn't mean we should. Hey, I'm Miranda Cosgrove and welcome to my STEM Loft, where one of the elevator buttons is a skull and crossbones and I really want to press it. You likely prefer writing notes, scrolling social media, and hitting a baseball either with your right or left hand. 99% of us are either right or left-handed, making it a lot easier to do things with one side of our bodies. And the other side, well, let's just say it doesn't work quite as well. But humans aren't the only ones with a preference like this. Many other things in our universe like DNA and proteins also have a handedness. Now, what if we could change that handedness? This concept is called mirror life. The handedness of the building blocks of life is known as chirality. When a chiral object is laid on top of its mirror image, no matter how it's rotated, it won't perfectly line up. Think again of your hands. They're mirror images of each other. However, no matter how I rotate them, they can't be perfectly superimposed on top of each other. You may have experienced this when trying to put your left hand's glove on your right hand or your right hand's on your left. I wouldn't say this is my most stylish look. DNA is naturally right-handed, meaning its classic DNA double-helix shape twists to the right. On the other hand, proteins are left-handed. Some molecules like tartrate, which can be found in wine or is sometimes added to food, have left or right-handed forms. Each molecule's chirality makes a big impact on how it functions. Louis Pasteur is most famous for his creation of pasteurization, a process that kills harmful pathogens in things like milk, but he's also considered the father of molecular chirality. He discovered chirality when he separated left and right-handed tartrate crystal shapes from each other back in 1847. But what would happen if we could change the chirality of left or right-handed microbes and flip them around into something else?

title: Towards Calibrating Prompt Tuning of Vision- Language Models - CVPR 2026
transcription: I am presenting our work, towards calibrating prompt tuning of vision-language models. This work focuses on improving the reliability of prompt-tuned CLIP models. Our main goal is not only to improve accuracy, but also to make the model's confidence more trustworthy. Prompt tuning is widely used because it adapts CLIP efficiently without updating the full model. However, most existing methods mainly focus on classification accuracy. In real-world applications, accuracy alone is not enough. A model must also know how confident it should be. If a model gives high confidence to wrong predictions, it becomes risky in areas such as medical imaging, autonomous systems, and safety-critical AI. Therefore, models' predicted confidence should equal to the true likelihood or model predicted accuracy. This will ensure that the model's predicted confidence is calibrated. Post-hoc calibration can adjust confidence after training, but it cannot prevent embedding drift caused during prompt tuning. Our key observation is that prompt tuning creates a dual miscalibration problem. For base classes, the model often becomes underconfident because the logit margins are reduced. For novel classes, the model becomes overconfident because the margins become inflated or unstable. The reliability diagrams and margin analysis show that margin behavior affects base and novel classes differently. Therefore, we need a train-time method that controls both logit margins and text embedding geometry, which preserves CLIP geometry by preventing prompt-induced semantic drift and stabilizes class relations, reducing overconfident wrong predictions, thereby lowering calibration error. To solve this, we propose two complementary losses. First, the mean variance margin loss stabilizes the logit gap between the ground-truth class and the strongest incorrect class. This helps improve confidence separation. Second, the text moment matching loss preserves CLIP's original text embedding geometry by matching the distribution of tuned text embeddings with frozen CLIP embeddings. The total loss combines cross-entropy, margin regularization, and moment matching. Together, they reduce base class underconfidence and novel class overconfidence. Margin loss alone is useful, but it can still create high-confidence wrong predictions, especially on novel classes. This happens because if the model predicts the wrong class, increasing the margin can make that wrong prediction even more confident. Moment matching solves this by preserving semantic geometry. So, margin improves discriminability, while moment matching prevents semantic drift. Their combination gives better calibration, especially for novel classes. We evaluate the method on 11 datasets: ImageNet, Caltech-101, Pets, Cars, Flowers...

The speaker explains the risks of miscalibrated models in safety-critical applications like autonomous systems and medical imaging. He highlights a "dual miscalibration problem," where base classes become underconfident and novel classes become overconfident. To address this, he proposes two complementary losses: the "mean variance margin loss" and the "text moment matching loss," explaining how they work together to stabilize logit margins and preserve text embedding geometry. Finally, he mentions evaluating the method across 11 datasets, including ImageNet, Caltech 101, Pets, Cars, and Flowers. The audio is high quality, with no noticeable background noise.

transcription: Let's talk about the PLAUD NOTE and the PLAUD NOTE Pro which I actually have right here. title: Wearable Technology Helps Local Father Born Legally Blind See with 20/20 Clarity!
transcription: Oh, well, good morning and welcome back. A local father from the San Fernando Valley was born legally blind, but all thanks to eyewear technology, he can now see with 20/20 clarity in real time. Here to tell us about the life-changing technology that allowed him to see his children's faces clearly for the first time is local dad Cosmo Moor. Good morning, thanks for joining us. Good morning, thanks for having me. Tell us about being born legally blind. How impaired was your vision before wearing this technology? I was born with optic nerve atrophy, and so it's uncorrectable because glasses fix eyeball issues. This is the nerve that connects the eyeball to the brain, so nothing can be done. Stem cell research maybe one day, but we're behind on that. So my vision's 20 over 400. What a normally-sighted person can see at 400 feet, I have to get up at 20 to see. And, for example, my phone has the accessibility turned up to maximum text. I still have to hold it an inch away from my face to see it. And so with these glasses, it has a camera here, feeds it to the screens. It can zoom up to 24 times and with it, I can see 20/20. That's incredible. You found the creators of eSight, which is a wearable technology, by the way, you see it on your face now, and suddenly you were able to see your children's faces clearly for the first time. Take us back to that moment and how you said at that point, "I got to be all in with this company and I'll work with them." Yeah. Um, I tried out the first generation eSight in 2013. It was much bigger, the controller was wired and it was huge, and it was $15,000, and so I passed on that, but I stayed following the company and in 2017, that's when I got an eSight 3. This is the fifth generation device. Wow. And, to see somebody's face, well, I need to be 18 in away, and that doesn't happen very often other than my wife. And so the first time I put this on and I could zoom in and see their faces clearly, one of my favorite memories was going to the zoo with my then 3-year-old, and he got on the merry-go-round. And normally, I just waved to daddy, "Yeah, I can't see you. I hope that's you." And I could track his face the whole way around when he went to the merry-go-round and that was cool seeing the joy

title: Reclaiming the lost art of listening to music
transcription: To Connor Knighton now and an invitation to just listen. And we're going to ask that when we drop the needle we refrain from any conversation. This is a listening environment. Seattle Shibuya Hi-Fi is a listening bar. Our guests can chat and sip cocktails in the lounge. They then leave their drinks and their shoes behind as they settle into the back room to enjoy full-length albums in a communal setting. An evening might feature anything from Björk to David Bowie. I love David Bowie cuz I've got, oh my gosh, my Bowie tattoo. I had to be here. It's the closest thing I could get to a David Bowie concert. These curated sessions, around 80 a month, regularly sell out. People are buying $20 tickets to listen to albums they could hear at home for free. That seems to me to be something that people are really rediscovering, that pleasure and the beauty of focus and intentional listening. Quentin Ertel is the co-owner of Shibuya Hi-Fi, which takes its name from a neighborhood in Tokyo. In Japan, listening bars, often called jazz kissas, started gaining popularity back in the 1930s. But similar venues have exploded in the US in recent years, popping up everywhere from Minnesota to Missouri to Colorado. There is a new wave of like these kind of listening bars especially in the West. Oh, cool. Artist and engineer Devon Turnbull designs high-end, handmade audio equipment for his company Ojas. While his speakers often end up in private living rooms, he's also created larger public listening rooms. The Smithsonian's Cooper Hewitt Museum in New York is currently showcasing what Turnbull has deemed his Hi-Fi Pursuit Listening Room Dream No. 3, installed in what was once Andrew Carnegie's private library. Pursuit is a really important part of the title. I am not here to say that I have made the ultimate sound system. This is about my pursuit as a builder, as someone who's passionate about building audio equipment and listening to music through it. Turnbull works out of a warehouse in Brooklyn's Navy Yard. title: Investigative Journalist Tom O'Neill on CIA's MKUltra Mind-Control Program
transcription: Almost 50 years ago, the last congressional hearings into MK-Ultra took place just a short walk from here in the Dirksen Senate Office Building. At those hearings convened in August and September of 1977, representatives of the CIA told Congress and the American people that its 25-year effort to control human behavior had been a colossal failure. Because I believe Congress was never told the truth about what this program actually achieved. In fact, I believe the agency misled Congress in 1977 when it characterized MK-Ultra as a failure. My name is Tom O'Neill and in 1999, I was accepted, I accepted a magazine assignment to write a story about murders committed by a group of hippies called the Manson family. For those unfamiliar with this horrific episode of American history, in the summer of 1969, four young people acting on the orders of a cult leader named Charles Manson went to the home of movie director Roman Polanski and murdered everyone they found there, including his eight-and-a-half-month pregnant wife, the actress Sharon Tate. The victims were complete strangers to the, to their killers. The following night, Manson's followers murdered another couple in the same grisly fashion. At the time I accepted the assignment, I had never heard of MK-Ultra, and I wouldn't for another two years, after I'd missed countless deadlines, lost the assignment, and fallen down a nightmarish rabbit hole trying to answer the question I couldn't quite shake. How had Manson, a barely literate ex-con, acquired the ability to persuade ordinary young people to murder complete strangers simply because he had told them to? The pursuit of that answer, the pursuit of the answer to that question led me to Dr. Louis Jolyon West, known to his friends as Jolly. West was one of the most influential psychiatrists in America. During his career, he crossed paths with some of the most controversial events of the 20th century, including the Patty Hearst kidnapping case and the aftermath of the John F. Kennedy assassination investigation.

Um, Mike, first take us through what you and your colleagues are reporting today. title: Nolan Wells' death: FBI probes threats
transcription: Welcome back. The FBI is investigating threats against the people who were with Nolan Wells in the hours before the Mississippi teen vanished and was found dead. Wells, 18, disappeared July 4th after joining friends on a boat trip to Horn Island, a barrier island off Mississippi's Gulf Coast. Search crews scoured the area for two days before a National Park Service Ranger found his remains on the island's northwestern tip on July 6th. Wells' friends returned to the mainland that July afternoon without him, but Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter previously said investigators believed Wells chose to stay on the island. It wasn't until later that night that his mother learned that he was missing from one of Wells' friends and reported it to authorities. Mississippi's Department of Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell said Wednesday that the FBI is investigating threats made against public officials, the people who were with Wells before he vanished, and their families. Michelle Thomas is now joining us here on LiveNOW from FOX. Michelle, thank you so much for taking the time to talk with us. Thanks so much for having me. So, we talk about this case. The FBI is now investigating threats connected to the case. So, what kind of threats can become federal crimes, and why would the FBI get involved here? Well, anytime there's a threat regarding anyone's person, placing them in immediate harm, there's going to be an investigation. But here, they may also be looking for racially charged threats, given sort of the backdrop of what we've heard about in the public scrutiny, in the public eye, and with the backdrop in history of Mississippi. People are concerned about this case because of sort of the racial makeup and so forth. So, if there are any kind of threats along those lines, there's going to be an investigation, and possibly a federal one. And when we talk about authorities, you know, saying that witnesses, public officials, even family members have received some type of threat here or there, how can that affect an active criminal investigation that can be happening? Well, any kind of law enforcement is going to follow any leads and they're going to try to track any any type of threat because they don't want there to be either witness intimidation or witness coercion. They want to make sure that they're able to preserve the evidence and witness testimony, and that persons with knowledge are able to come forward without feeling fearful. So, it can taint an investigation, and possibly a forthcoming trial, if there are constant threats and people are afraid to come forward with the information needed to solve what happened to Nolan Wells.

transcription: Each deeply reported account of self-dealing from the Trump White House seems to get more brazen than the one that came before it. The New York Times has now reviewed a number of federal filings and is out with an extraordinary piece of investigative reporting that details the latest way that Donald Trump's family and allies appear to be profiting off Donald Trump's policy decisions as president. It involves a billion-dollar mining deal with Kazakhstan and one that both Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's sons stand to profit from. In a meeting last September, Donald Trump and Howard Lutnick secured a deal with the leader of Kazakhstan to give a little-known American company now called Kaz Resources access to one of the world's largest untapped reserves of tungsten. It's a crucial rare earth mineral. Here's where the apparent self-dealing comes in, according to the New York Times. Weeks after that meeting, quote, "investors with a firm called Dominari Securities, which is housed at Trump Tower in New York and partly owned by the president's two eldest sons, Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, joined with other partners to take a 20% stake in the corporate entity related to the Kazakhstan project." Around the same time, Cantor Fitzgerald, an investment company controlled by Howard Lutnick's family and overseen by his sons Brandon and Kyle Lutnick, helped one of the lead investors working with Dominari on the Kazakh deal raise $210 million in new capital for a related entity. Such rounds of fundraising typically net Cantor millions of dollars in fees. The deal was, quote, "ultimately signed on November 6th, six days after the investment involving the Trump sons and their partners, which was not publicly disclosed at the time." As the New York Times reports, this continues a pattern of self-enrichment in the Trump administration that has few precedents in American history. When asked for statements, both the White House and the Commerce Department rejected any suggestion that the Trump administration was improperly mixing government actions with family business. Trump's sons both denied being involved in the specifics of the deal. Eric Trump claimed they were passive investors. A Cantor Fitzgerald spokesperson said that company's executives were not involved in discussions related to government funding.

transcription: This is breaking news. දැන් ලැබුණු විශේෂ පුවතක් වෙත අවධානය යොමු කරනවා. පාස්කු ඉරිදින ත්‍රස්ත ප්‍රහාරය සම්බන්ධව රාජකාරී වගකීම පැහැර හරිමින් මරණ සිදු වීමට ආධාර අනුබල දීමේ චෝදනාවට වරදකරු බවට පත් කළ හිටපු පොලිස්පති පූජිත් ජයසුන්දරට විශේෂ ත්‍රිපුද්ගල මහාධිකරණය මරණ දඩුවම නියම කළා. නඩුව විභාගයට ගැනුනේ ප්‍රියන්ත ලියනගේ, තිලකරත්න බණ්ඩාර සහ විරාජ් වීරසූරිය යන විශේෂ ත්‍රිපුද්ගල මහාධිකරණ විනිසුරුවරුන් හමුවේ. සභාපති විනිසුරු ප්‍රියන්ත ලියනගේ සහ තිලකරත්න බණ්ඩාර යන විනිසුරුවරුන් මෙහිදී පූජිත් ජයසුන්දර වරදකරු බවට තීන්දු කළ අතර විරාජ් වීරසූරිය විනිසුරුවරයාගේ තීන්දුව වූයේ අදාළ චෝදනා සාධාරණ සැකයෙන් ඔබ්බට ඔප්පු කිරීමට අසමත් බවයි. විනිසුරු මඩුල්ලේ බහුතර තීන්දුව අනුව චෝදනා 855කින් 854කට හිටපු පොලිස්පති පූජිත් ජයසුන්දර වරදකරු බවට තීන්දු කෙරුණා. හිටපු ආරක්ෂක ලේකම් හේමසිරි ප්‍රනාන්දු සම්බන්ධ තීන්දුවද ප්‍රකාශයට පත් කිරීමට නියමිතයි. යළිත් එම පුවත, පාස්කු ඉරිදින ත්‍රස්ත ප්‍රහාරය සම්බන්ධව රාජකාරී වගකීම පැහැර හරිමින් මරණ සිදු වීමට ආධාර අනුබල දීමේ චෝදනාවට වරදකරු බවට පත් කළ හිටපු පොලිස්පති පූජිත් ජයසුන්දරට විශේෂ ත්‍රිපුද්ගල මහාධිකරණය මරණ දඩුවම නියම කළා. නඩුව විභාගයට ගැනුනේ ප්‍රියන්ත ලියනගේ, තිලකරත්න බණ්ඩාර සහ විරාජ් වීරසූරිය යන විශේෂ ත්‍රිපුද්ගල මහාධිකරණ විනිසුරුවරුන් හමුවේ. සභාපති විනිසුරු ප්‍රියන්ත ලියනගේ සහ තිලකරත්න බණ්ඩාර යන විනිසුරුවරුන් මෙහිදී පූජිත් ජයසුන්දර වරදකරු බවට තීන්දු කළ අතර විරාජ් වීරසූරිය විනිසුරුවරයාගේ තීන්දුව වූයේ අදාළ චෝදනා සාධාරණ සැකයෙන් ඔබ්බට ඔප්පු කිරීමට අසමත් බවයි. විනිසුරු මඩුල්ලේ බහුතර තීන්දුව අනුව චෝදනා 855කින් 854කට හිටපු පොලිස්පති පූජිත් ජයසුන්දර වරදකරු බවට තීන්දු කෙරුණා. හිටපු ආරක්ෂක ලේකම් හේමසිරි ප්‍රනාන්දු සම්බන්ධ තීන්දුවද ප්‍රකාශයට පත් කිරීමට නියමිතයි. ජෙෆ්රි. ස්තූතියි ඔමායා. விசேட செய்தி ஊடாக உங்கள் அனைவரையும் நாங்கள் நேரடியாகச் சந்திக்கிறோம். உயிர்த்த ஞாயிறு தாக்குதல் தொடர்பில் கடமையைத் தவறியதால் ஏற்பட்ட உயிரிழப்புகளுக்குக் காரணமாக அமைந்தமை தொடர்பில் சுமத்தப்பட்ட குற்றச்சாட்டுக்களுக்கு முன்னாள் பொலிஸ் மா அதிபர் பூஜித் ஜயசுந்தரவுக்கு விசேட மூவரடங்கிய மேல் நீதிமன்றத்தினால் மரண தண்டனை விதிக்கப்பட்டிருக்கிறது. பிரியந்த லியனகே, திலகரத்ன பண்டார, விராஜ் வீரசூரிய விசேட மூவரடங்கிய மேல் நீதிமன்ற நீதிபதிகளால் இந்தத் தீர்ப்பு வழங்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. அந்த விசேட செய்தியினை மீண்டும் அறியத் தருகிறோம். உயிர்த்த ஞாயிறு தாக்குதல் transcription: दोस्तों अगर आप भी एक न्यू स्मार्टफोन लेने का मन बना चुके हो तो थोड़ा सा रुक जाओ क्योंकि अगले महीने यानी अगस्त के महीने में बहुत सारे तगड़े-तगड़े स्मार्टफोंस लॉन्च होने वाले हैं जो शायद आपका मन बदल दें और आपको एक बेहतर स्मार्टफोन मिल जाए तो वीडियो को एंड तक ज़रूर देखना और दोस्तों इस वीडियो में हमने सभी फोंस को रैंकिंग वाइस ऐड किया है यानी सबसे पहले हम कम बजट से स्टार्ट करेंगे और बढ़ते-बढ़ते हाई बजट तक जाएंगे साथ ही सभी फोंस के एक्सपेक्टेड स्पेसिफिकेशन, प्राइसिंग और लॉन्च डेट को भी जानेंगे तो वीडियो काफी इंटरेस्टिंग होने वाली है मेक श्योर की वीडियो को एंड तक जरूर देखना बाकी बिना किसी देरी के शुरू करते हैं आज के इस वीडियो को। तो देखो सबसे पहला स्मार्टफोन आने वाला है वनप्लस की तरफ से N6X बेसिकली दोस्तों यह एक बजट सेगमेंट स्मार्टफोन होगा जो कि मेरे ख्याल से अराउंड 20,000 में लॉन्च हो सकता है एंड ये आपको अगस्त के स्टार्टिंग में ही देखने को मिल जाएगा। इसके फीचर्स की बात करें तो इधर आपको 6.8 इंच का HD+ LCD बड़ा डिस्प्ले मिलेगा साथ ही 8000 mAh की बड़ी बैटरी जो आपको 2 दिन तक का बैकअप निकाल के दे सकता है वहीं 50 मेगापिक्सल का मेन कैमरा सेंसर और चिपसेट के बारे में अभी उतना कुछ पता नहीं है बाकी डिज़ाइन तो वनप्लस का अच्छा ही रहता है। देखो भाई ओवरऑल फोन अच्छा है लेकिन प्राइस हैक के कारण डिस्प्ले और परफॉर्मेंस में कॉस्ट कटिंग की गई है। इसके बाद अगला फोन आता है इंफिनिक्स की तरफ से Hot 70 Pro जिसमें आपको मीडियाटेक डाइमेंसिटी का 7100 5G वाला चिपसेट मिलेगा और ये आउट ऑफ द बॉक्स एंड्राइड 15 विद एक्स ओएस के साथ आएगा। वही डिस्प्ले में 6.76 इंचेज का FHD+ पंचहोल पैनल मिलेगा जो की अप टू 144Hz के हायर रिफ्रेश रेट को सपोर्ट करता है और ये IP68 के डस्ट प्लस वाटर रेजिस्टेंस को भी सपोर्ट करता है बाकी कैमरे के लिए बैक में 50 मेगापिक्सल का प्राइमरी मेन सेंसर और 8 मेगापिक्सल का सेल्फी सरल लेंस दिया गया है जो की ठीक-ठाक क्वालिटी के इमेजेस को क्लिक करता है आपका काम चल जाएगा एंड And every day they see President Trump in the Oval Office, it's like another scratch at their scabbed over egos. They're disgusted by you, one of the 77 million Americans who voted for Trump. But they shouldn't be mad at the people, the media should be mad at themselves for not understanding the country better. But if you thought that the release of the Fauci diaries would have forced the establishment press to have a moment, just a brief moment of self-reflection, well, you'd be wrong. The documents, released by Republican Senator Rand Paul, include Fauci's reflections about being invited to A-list parties, calls with Barbra Streisand, but also some uncertainty about the origin of COVID. Oh, some uncertainty. No. No, no uncertainty. Well, as lame as that intro is, it's better than some of the other networks through yesterday morning. title: How to Tell What's Real and What's AI-Generated on Social Media
transcription: Midnight souls again? Come on, Gus, people are sleeping. Has your social media feed started to look a little off? Tell me I'm not hallucinating right now. Fake celebrity endorsements, news reports, doorbell camera footage and more that all look real at first swipe, but have a certain eeriness. Or maybe you've seen videos that are a bit more overtly fake. Yep, it's really me, Bigfoot. Like the many clips of animals doing seemingly impossible things, these videos generated by AI tools from Meta, Google, OpenAI and more are spreading on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and X at a rapid pace. Every other scroll, it is some AI-generated like influencer. Dubbed AI slop, some of these clips are meant to make us laugh, like Marilyn Monroe here. While others are out to spread misinformation in a world already struggling with claims of fake news. You will be fooled by an AI photo this week, and you probably already have been and you didn't know it. We have not come to terms with what this means for society. Celebrities like Keanu Reeves having to grapple with AI deepfakes. How disconcerting is that for you? Um well, I mean, it's not a lot of fun. Even Al has been the target of AI videos trying to dupe shoppers. Reversing my hypertension in just 3 months. I don't have hypertension. It can be easy to spot the more outlandish AI clips, but what about something more believable? Like a dog cuddling up to a baby, a grandma dancing at a barbecue, or a harrowing bodycam video. I got you. Pull your leg, pull your leg. Even AI fakes designed to make you feel good, to tug on your heartstrings. These videos are turning feeds into a mix of real life content and computer made footage, and some users are tired of it. I don't know what the solution is, but this technology should never have existed in the first place. So how can the average social media user separate fact from fiction? So, we're going to show you what is out there, what is fake. The team at Corridor Digital, a production studio with more than 7 million subscribers on YouTube, put some special people to the test.

title: BREAKING NEWS: LeBron James signs with the Philadelphia 76ers! | First Take
transcription: We have breaking news here on First Take. According to Shams, LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $80 million deal with a player option. This comes after more than 20 days since he announced that he will be leaving the Los Angeles Lakers to play the next chapter of his career somewhere else. Stephen A., we knew it was coming soon, we did not know it was coming today. Your initial reaction to LeBron joining forces with Jaylen Brown and company in Philly? Shock, because I thought that if he was going back East, he would go home. That he wouldn't dangle his pres- his- his availability in the face of the Cleveland Cavaliers, and then go somewhere else. For him to choose the Philadelphia 76ers, this is a shock amongst shockers. And I think that this speaks to Bob Myers, the for- the architect, the former four-time champion executive for the Golden State Warriors, being in Philly now and having him there, who went out and pulled off a heist as far as most of us are concerned in getting Jaylen Brown. So now you got Jaylen Brown, okay, who's big-time, obviously, with Tyrese Maxey, who's big-time, you got him with VJ Edgecombe, who is uh who shined as a rookie and got tremendous potential. And now you're looking at it, if Joel Embiid is 50%, I mean, if he can give you anything during the playoffs, the Philadelphia 76ers could win the championship. I think this right here puts the Philadelphia 76ers right there with the New York Knicks as the favorites in the Eastern Conference to come out of the East and represent the Eastern Conference in the NBA Finals. That's how big this move is because LeBron is a savant, his basketball IQ is off the charts, and you combine that with the greatness of a Jaylen Brown and a Tyrese Maxey, with the leadership that Bob Myers has emanating from above as the executive for this team. I don't think there's any question, Philadelphia 76ers, I'm shocked by this. The Philadelphia 76ers are now in play to be a championship favorite. Well, I watched it started with Scotland, and all of a sudden, they're doing things that nobody's ever seen with the bagpipes, and it was beautiful, and it just went to every country. And they're realizing what a great country this is. Uh, we're the hottest country in the world right now for, this helped, but for a lot of other reasons. We have trillions of dollars being spent in the United States. They're coming from all over the world, and they're spending their money here. And we've never had a period of, I call it the golden age of America. It's amazing. Uh, but I'll tell you, the World Cup, uh, you know, this is your deal, right? The World Cup. But the World Cup has really helped. It's been, uh, it's been tremendous. It's gotten the world, the word out, Mm. and nobody thought it was possible. I heard numbers that it's, uh, many times what's ever been done before, so that's great. Uh, you're such a sports fan. We just had UFC at the White House, we have the Olympics coming, and a big one on FOX, the Freedom 250 Indy car race. How much are you looking forward to it? Well, Roger Penske is a friend of mine, and he's been trying to get this race for 25 years, and he's had no luck in Congress. Congress is a tough place. And he said, "I've come here 212 times," or some, some massive number like that, uh, over many, many years, and he always went home empty-handed. He's not used to that. He came to see me. He said, "I saw Trump for 15 minutes, and we had a deal done." And not only done, it's going to be the best track you can imagine, down Pennsylvania Avenue, around the Capitol. That race is going to be something, and I think they have 400,000 people already signed up. And we had UFC, which was their record. They've never done, I think it was the all-time fight record, in front of the White House, at the front door of the White House. And some fights that were incredible. When you look at, uh, those last couple of fights, they were incredible, actually. Back to this FIFA World Cup, I got to ask: Argentina-Spain, Yeah. give me a prediction. transcription:
The clock is ticking on President Trump's 48-hour ultimatum he issued to Iran, warning last night that the US will strike its power plants if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened. And we should start hearing the sirens, uh, in about 2 minutes now. So, when we hear the sirens start coming, usually what we get, uh, out of Iran these days are the cluster bombs. And the reason you get the cluster bombs is they're just they're effective in terms of getting through, uh, the Israeli air defenses. And when I say cluster bomb, uh, what I'm talking about is a warhead that's made up of dozens of little bombs, and when that's intercepted by the air defenses, it'll break up, uh, into dozens of bomblets, and the bomblets still get through. And we've seen them be very effective in terms of hurting people on the ground or destroying property because those bomblets get through. Uh, what we saw yesterday was an exception because those were ballistic missiles with big 1,000-pound warheads. For the most part, those big warheads aren't getting through; they get intercepted. Last night, two of them got through into Dimona and Arad. Uh, the IDF did their investigation, and they simply determined that there wasn't, uh, a new type of weapon that was effective in terms of getting through, uh, and there wasn't a failure of the system. It's just a fact that you're shooting missiles out of sky, which is a very difficult thing to do. So, we're keeping an eye on the skies to the east of us right now because that's where we, uh, expect the missiles to appear. That's the direction, uh, par- pardon me, where the, uh, uh, where the missiles come through, uh, and then, hopefully, we'll see the interceptors launch and get after them. So, that's the situation right now, and this is a drill that the people here in Israel, uh, are repeating every day, multiple times a day. Uh, you get the alerts over your phone, that's the period we're in right now. Once you start hearing the sirens wail in the background, that's an indication that the missiles are getting close.

title: DETAILS: US deploys laser tech against Iranian drones
transcription: Iranian Shahed drones pose a real threat to US forces and our Gulf allies, so the Pentagon is now deploying new laser technology to help take them down. Brian Llenas joins us live from our London bureau. Good morning, Brian. Good morning, Lawrence, Ainsley, and Brian. You know, the US Navy is equipped with two laser systems that are capable of taking down these Iranian drones, the ODIN and the HELIOS. Now, the ODIN was spotted in a CENTCOM video that was released at the beginning of Operation Epic Fury on board the Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer. You can see it there in that box. Now, the ODIN blinds drones, firing an infrared beam that overwhelms drone sensors, causing it to crash or fail. There are at least two destroyers in Epic Fury that are equipped with the ODIN. Now, the HELIOS is a high-energy laser beam with a high-powered sensor that tracks, blows up drones and missiles in the air by igniting the fuel. Now, the HELIOS is not confirmed to be deployed in Epic Fury. It's only known to be on a US ship that was last seen in the Indo-Pacific in Japan. Now, these technologies are vital in defending against Iran's drone attacks. Iran has fired off four times as many Shahed drones as ballistic missiles attacking our Gulf Arab allies. Now, Iran's biggest advantage is that these drones cost $35,000 to make, but one Patriot missile fired to shoot down these drones costs $4 million per missile. Now, these laser technologies cost pennies per shot and perhaps they're part of the reason why the US says it is not concerned about running out of munitions in this war. We've had a number of new capabilities being fielded. Obviously, I'm not going to talk about it from an operational perspective of what those are. But, I think you have seen over a period of time, us kind of get on the other side of this cost curve on drones in general. Now meantime, Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says he has accepted a request by the US and our Gulf allies to help in countering Iran's drones. Ukraine has become an expert of taking down Shahed drones fired by Russia. This is an ad from a Ukrainian company, Wild Hornets, and it shows the Sting, a low-cost quadcopter interceptor that successfully takes down these drones. Ukraine has also used the Octopus. It's an AI-powered drone interceptor developed by Ukraine, US, and the UK. It can track drones at night using AI and even go past electronic jamming. The Gulf states are reportedly, guys, discussing using the Octopus to defend themselves with these drone interceptors. They cost about $5,000 to make, much cheaper than the $4 million Patriot missile, which will ensure that our Gulf allies and the US can stay in this fight for as long as they need.

title: Why Christopher Nolan shot "The Odyssey" on IMAX film
transcription: 60 minutes overtime. 3, 2, 1, action. Director Christopher Nolan has made some of the most spectacular films of the 21st century. The Dark Knight, Inception, Interstellar, Dunkirk, and Oppenheimer. With each new film, the scale and ambition of Nolan's storytelling seems to reach new heights. So, it's only fitting that his latest coming to theaters this July takes on a nearly 3,000-year-old Greek epic, The Odyssey. Let's go! Matt Damon plays King Odysseus in The Odyssey. This is his third film with Nolan. I think what separates him from other directors is the stories he wants to tell are incredibly ambitious and the way he wants to tell them is incredibly ambitious because he wants to do it all in-camera. In this case, he wanted to do it 100% in IMAX, which had never been done. And that wasn't even announced because we didn't know if we could do it. The Odyssey is the first feature film shot entirely with IMAX film. Each frame has resolution or image quality up to three times higher than digital. Action! The IMAX camera has to stop and be reloaded every two and a half minutes or so. Thank you. Because the format is so large, that's the most film the camera can hold at one time. Another challenge, when the cameras are rolling, they're loud. The heavy duty mechanism that pulls the film past the shutter sounds like a sewing machine in a fight with a stapler. It's a really loud camera, so for intimate scenes, for for instance, if we were going to shoot this scene, that would have been impossible in IMAX up until, you know, a year ago. Camera's too loud. Camera's just much too loud, the audio would never would never work. For the Odyssey,

title: The WNBA has 'no integrity': Dan Dakich
transcription: WNBA star Sophie Cunningham is not backing down from her opposition to biological men in women's sports. And her supporters are not staying quiet either. Another rally took place outside today's Fever/Lynx game. Her coach called the attention frustrating and a reporter tried to get Cunningham's teammate to weigh in. There's a frustration, of course, because we want to we want to talk about basketball. But I also understand, like, this is this is part of our growth edge as a league. We speaking of the outside noise, Sophie your teammate. Sophie came out with... Oh, thank you. Have a good day. Outkick host, Dan Dakich, joins me now. Uh Dan, why why do so many uh members of the league seem not to want to talk about this? Well, because you get excluded, you get bullied, you get harassed, you have marches. Today, Cheryl Reeve, the coach of the Minnesota Lynx playing against Sophie Cunningham, wore a shirt that said, "Trans kids belong" in reference to Sophie Cunningham saying boys should stay out of women's basketball. And I would argue, okay, what's the end of that shirt? Nobody's arguing trans kids don't belong. Sophie Cunningham simply is saying that boys should stay out of girls' locker rooms and compete against boys. And others, including, unbelievably, Stephanie White, the coach of the Fever, doesn't understand that nobody would have ever heard of Stephanie White. I live in Indiana. She's an Indiana legend. If boys were allowed to play against Stephanie White at her little high school in rural Indiana or at Purdue, we would've never heard of her. She would've never had these opportunities if boys were allowed. But the bullying, the harassment goes on in that league. The league has no integrity. The commissioners are a joke. And so, people are afraid. Yeah, it's it's not like uh LeBron James just signed on to join the Fever. Uh, you know, there is a reason they call it women's NBA, right?
caption: The audio is a segment from a news broadcast discussing the controversy surrounding WNBA player Sophie Cunningham's stance on transgender athletes in women's sports. It begins with a male news anchor introducing the topic, followed by a brief press conference clip. In the clip, a female coach expresses frustration but views the situation as part of the league's growth, followed by a teammate abruptly ending an interview when asked about Cunningham. The anchor then interviews sports commentator Dan Dakich, who speaks passionately and critically about the league, alleging that players are bullied into silence. Dakich criticizes other coaches, like Cheryl Reeve for wearing a shirt supporting trans kids, and Stephanie White, arguing that allowing biological males would destroy opportunities for female athletes. The segment concludes with the anchor and Dakich sharing a lighthearted agreement about the league being named the 'Women's' NBA.

तो मैच जो होगा वो रनगिरी दाम्बुला स्टेडियम में खेला जाएगा। रनगिरी दाम्बुला स्टेडियम, जहां पर फिलहाल के लिए पिछला मैच खेला गया था दोनों टीमों का और आपने देखा कि वो मैच काफी अच्छा और बेहतर तरीके से पिछला वाला रहा था दोनों टीम के बीच में। पाकिस्तान पहले इनिंग में बहुत अच्छा 170 के ऊपर का स्कोर करी थी और 170 स्कोर करने के साथ ही साथ इस टीम ने बहुत बढ़िया परफॉर्मेंस बल्लेबाजी में करके दिखाया। यह अलग बात है कि बॉलिंग में टीम का परफॉर्मेंस उतना अच्छा नहीं हो सका था और टीम का थोड़ा परफॉर्मेंस बॉलिंग में खराब गया, लेकिन ओवरऑल टीम ने बहुत बढ़िया तरीके से दोनों ने खेला था। दोनों ही टीमों का परफॉर्मेंस काफी हद तक अच्छा, जबरदस्त तरीके से देखने को मिला। उम्मीद है आज के मैच में भी दोनों टीमें बढ़िया तरीके से ही खेलेगी और जबरदस्त परफॉर्मेंस दोस्तों देखने को मिलते नजर आएंगे। जो पॉसिबल प्लेइंग इलेवन दोनों टीमों की है और टॉस हो चुका है। टॉस का अपडेट ये देख सकते हैं आप पाकिस्तान टॉस जीत के बल्लेबाजी करने के लिए गई है जबकि पिछले मैच में फर्स्ट बैटिंग करके और पाकिस्तान की टीम हारती नजर आई थी पिछले मैच में परफॉर्मेंस जो देखने को मिलता नजर आया था टीम का। तो जितना बेहतर होना चाहिए था वैसा नहीं देखने को मिला था, समझ रहे हैं ना? इस तरीके से गया था, लेकिन अब आज के मुकाबले में देखेंगे कि टीम का क्या परफॉर्मेंस रहता है। तो टॉस जीत करके फर्स्ट बैटिंग करने का फैसला इसके तरफ से फिलहाल के लिए आज के मुकाबले में नजर आया है। अब ओवरऑल देखते हैं आज क्या कर पाएगी। लेकिन जो पॉसिबल प्लेइंग इलेवन दोनों टीमों की नजर आ रही है, उसमें जो-जो प्लेयर्स होने वाली हैं उनके नाम जरा से एक बार देख लेते हैं और जानने की कोशिश करेंगे कि कौन-कौन सी खिलाड़ी को आज के मैच में मौका दिया जा सकता है। टॉस अभी जस्ट आया ही है। श्रीलंका टीम के तरफ से इमेषा दुलानी, विश्मी गुणरत्ने, नॉटी, उसके अलावा हंसनी परेरा और काव्या कविंदी होगी, साथ ही साथ चमारी अटापट्टू, हर्षिता समरविक्रमा, कविशा दिलहारी होने वाली है, नीलाक्षी डी सिल्वा और साथ में एक प्लेयर रशमिका होगी, रशमिका के साथ-साथ सुगंदिका कुमारी, काव्या कविंदी, मालकी मदारा जैसी प्लेयर आपको नजर आने वाली है। तो ये तो हो गई दरअसल श्रीलंका की टीम। दूसरी तरफ चलते हैं और जानने की कोशिश करते हैं कि पाकिस्तान की जो पॉसिबल प्लेइंग इलेवन क्या है और क्या हो सकता है आज के मैच में। तो इनकी टीम के तरफ से शवाल जुल्फिकार होगी, ऐमा नसीर, आयशा जफर और सायरा जबीन, आयमा फातिमा, उसके अलावा इनकी टीम में महान एनी करके एक खिलाड़ी होगी और नाजिया अल्वी, मुनीबा अली जो टीम की कप्तान विकेटकीपर है, उम्मे हानी होगी, नशरा संधू होने वाली है, तूबा हसन होने वाली है और साथ ही साथ हुमना बिलाल करके खिलाड़ी आपको देखने को मिलती नजर आएगी। ये तो

title: EA SPORTS FC 27 | Official Gameplay Deep Dive
transcription: More player control, more fluidity, and more changes led by you. There's so much that's new to gameplay this year. We addressed AI defending, reinvented corners, reworked attacking runs, dribbling under pressure, and fluid one-twos. And of course, retuned fundamentals to reduce intercept-backs, rebalance play styles, and deliver on more of the improvements you care about most. Let's dive in, starting with something you've called out over and over: AI defending. Your feedback is clear: manual defending should be the best way to stop your opponent. So we've tackled that from a number of angles this year, taking power away from the AI and giving it to you when you are defending. You'll feel the difference as soon as you take control. Your player will jockey more responsively. You'll also have a larger tackling range, a larger interception range, and a larger blocking range when defending manually. For example, the AI isn't quick enough to cut off the angle and can't quite reach to make the interception. But when you take control, that quicker jockey can get you into position and you're able to reach farther to win the ball. We've also minimized AI auto-tackles in competitive gameplay. The AI will still be able to win the ball if your opponent dribbles right into them, but they'll almost never lunge for the ball or reach into a challenge. And, we've loosened teammate contain and team press in the defensive third. The AI will still get into solid defensive positions, but taking manual control will give you more tools to stop your opponent. We've also reinvented corners to reduce luck and continue to reward skill. In FC 25, corners are split into two phases. One to prepare your pass and one that gives you creative control over your run. Pick your spot and power up your cross. Then, you'll have a few seconds to lose your marker so you can time your run to arrive at the perfect moment. This unlocks so much set-piece creativity, and equal amounts of set-piece chaos we see in leagues around the world. In attack, you'll have more control over how your

transcription: Here we go! Yan ang pwersa na taglay! Grabe ito mga idol. Apat na beses pinabagsak ni Fajardo ang isang knockout artist sa loob lang ng isang minuto. Out of Agusan del Sur, Philippines. It's Miel Fajardo. Yabuki Masamichi! Laging sundan, huwag magpapahuli, pag-usapan ni Pakbakan. mga idol, tapos na ang paghihintay dahil may isa na namang Pinoy boxer na lalaban para sa World Championship. I feel like that I need that kind of creative input directly from myself to kind of give me that feeling of purpose. And, yeah, during this period, I was just not really enjoying my job, I was using a lot. I was using a lot at home. I had a flatmate, but I'd often just kind of come home and go into my bedroom and just use all night and go to work. It was pretty bleak. Um, COVID then came and all the venues closed. There was obviously lockdown, I got put on furlough. Um, not long after that, I had to furlough... Sorry, I had to make all of the staff redundant. Me and one other guy had to do all the redundancies over Zoom calls, which was brutal. You know, a lot of these people I'd worked with for many years and I considered a friend. So, to have to do that was really challenging mentally. Um. At the time, I was actually engaged to my ex and we were planning our wedding and we were also kind of saving for the future to like buy a house and stuff like that. And I remember asking my boss, "Do, you know, is there any chance that I'm going to be made redundant? You know, because I'm that's going to really put me in a difficult situation." And, and the words he said to me, I can still remember now. He said, "If the ship..."

और वो आपको लॉन्ग टर्म में मोटा मोटा भी करेगा। फैटी लिवर भी करेगा। डेफिनेटली मैं आपको बोलूंगा प्योर वीट की रोटी अगर हम बंद कर सकते हैं हमें कर देनी चाहिए। एंड सब्स्टिट्यूट इट विद? अगर आपको डायबिटीज है, ज्वार आपके लिए बहुत अच्छा है। आपको प्रोटीन बढ़ाना है बाजरा। मिलेट्स। यस, आपको आयरन डेफिसिएंसी है रागी। हम्म। की आप ना वीट पसंद करते हैं तो उसे मिक्स तो कर लो। हम्म हम्म। ग्लाइसेमिक इंडेक्स तो कम कर दो उसका। हम्म। जो इंसुलिन स्पाइक आ रही है। अम, ये जो मिलेट्स की बात हमने करी है। डू यू थिंक दे आल्सो अफेक्ट गट बैक्टीरिया डिफरेंटली एंड अफेक्ट योर स्टूल हेल्थ डिफरेंटली? फाइबर तो है ही ना। कॉम्प्लेक्स कार्बोहाइड्रेट्स और फाइबर तो हैं ही, बिल्कुल हैं। मतलब उस लेवल पे फाइबर नहीं है। फ्रूट्स के लेवल के फाइबर नहीं है, बट पार्टली फाइबर तो है इनमें। वीट से ज्यादा? वीट से ज्यादा है। बिल्कुल है। ओके। अ अब ये बताइए कि जितने सारे लोग वीट को पूरी तरह से छोड़ रहे हैं, अक्सर सेल्फ डायग्नोसिस की वजह से। दैट्स माय एंगल। हां। मैंने यह भी सुना है कि इफ यू कॉन्शियसली लीव वीट एंड यू जस्ट डोंट कीप इट इन योर डाइट तो यू डू बिकम ग्लूटेन सेंसिटिव जस्ट बिकॉज़ ऑफ़ डूइंग दैट। नहीं नहीं सर, ऐसा कुछ नहीं, साइंटिफिकली नहीं है। ग्लूटेन सर देखिए मैं आपको बताता हूं, मुझे ऐसा लगता है, मैंने काफी इसपे रिसर्च की कि ग्लूटन पता कैसे चलेगा जनता को? तो मेरे को याद आया कि नोवाक जोकोविच ने एक अपने इंटरव्यू में बोला था कि मैं ग्लूटन फ्री हूं। मुझे नहीं पता उसे सीलिएक डिजीज है की नहीं है। उसने बस ये बोला था कि मैं ग्लूटन फ्री हूं। हम्म हम्म। अब उसके पीछे उसका क्या मानना है मुझे नहीं पता। बट ऑब्वियसली ही इज़ अ गोट। मतलब ग्रेटेस्ट ऑफ़ ऑल टाइम हैं। आई थिंक रोजर फेडरर मेरा फेवरेट हुआ।

transcription: I know the to-do list today is getting out of this dang house. Guys know that I normally have USPS pick up my packages, but today we are going to the post office. My car also desperately needs a wash, which is probably pointless because the roads are so nasty, but I've just been thinking that I need a new car and I think if I wash it, I'll feel better. As you can see, we are dressed for full-blown summer today. All right, first up on the agenda is bagging up all of my packages so we can take them to the post office. All right, and I'm going to set all these over by the garage door so I can load them in the back of my car. Layne, if you're seeing this, I'm going to need you to move your truck. Also, Zach, I'm no mechanic, but I feel like your tractor tire might be flat. I'm not sure, but it appears that way. I'm telling you right now, this is why I feel like I need a new car. If I would just clean it, I'd be like, oh yeah, I do like my car. It is nice. But right now, I feel like I need to trade it in. I know that no part of that was aesthetic because my car is a filth ball. I know a pair of white tennis shoes hate to see me coming. Oh my gosh. Yep, that'll do it. I don't even know why I try.

title: Creative Reminder: The Video Journal Entry
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: What's up, everybody? Happy New Year. This is the first video of 2026. I'm so happy to be back on the camera. And in this video, I just really wanted to come on here and, in a way, create and post this, almost like a journal entry for myself, to like reflect on in July, and even in March, or towards the end of the year, to not give up on my work. And I really wanted to share that with you all as well. I want this to be a sign for you to not give up on your goals, your ideas, your content, your projects. And not just keep them up here, and to actually manifest them, put them out into the real space, and to really go from ideation to creation. And a lot of times, my ideas don't make it out of the basket, which is right here. They just stay in here. And then, sometimes, when I get in my moods and I reflect on that, I get sad because it's like, "Damn, I really be having some really good, dope ideas." And sometimes I get in my head because I'm like, "I don't know where to start," or, "This may be too big of a project," or, "I don't have help," or just letting things clog my brain. But I'm blessed to have community, God, just people around me who really want to see me win. And sometimes, even if I don't see it for myself, I'm happy to have those people to like remind me of who the heck I am, okay? Sometimes you need that, and I have that, and I need to be thankful for that. But I also want to be able to use that momentum to like, yeah, girl, you may have clients, you may have other people who want to work with you, or life hits hard, you know, but don't give up on the creation of everything, whether that's to intentionally rest, to read, to pause. It's like I don't want to give up on me. Like, even with right now, like creating this video, um, it's raining outside, I'm hungry, but I was like, "What better way to do it now? Your makeup's done, you got your camera, you got your lights, you got this." It's like, let's just do it, okay? Just do, because the more you do, the more you practice, the better things become. Ooh, hallelujah. Mmh. I'm challenging myself to show up

title: Diary Entry Writing | Minor Discourse 2.1 | Class 10 SSC English | LMR
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hey everyone, and welcome. Today, we're going to crack one of the easiest questions in your English exam, a question that can absolutely guarantee you full marks if you just know the secret. I know how stressful exams can be, but what if I told you there's one question that's not a trap, but actually your secret weapon for getting those marks in the bag? That's right, we are talking about the diary entry. Seriously, this can be the easiest question on the entire paper, but only if you know the simple formula that combines a little bit of format with a whole lot of feelings. So, what exactly is the diary entry? Well, think of it like you're just talking to yourself on paper. It's all about pouring out your personal feelings and what you've experienced. And because it's personal, it's always written in the first person, you know, using words like I, me and my. Okay, you ready for this? Let's dive into what I call the golden formula. It's like a simple, unbreakable code for success that's going to get you easy marks right from the start. All you have to do is memorize these five letters: D, D, T, S, B. That's it. It stands for Date, Day, Time, Salutation, and Body. This structure is your key. I mean, you'll literally be scoring points before you've even written a proper sentence. Okay, so let's break down that first part, the format. And honestly, this is where you're going to get the easiest marks in your entire exam. It is just this simple. At the top left of your page, you write the date, the day and the time, just like you see here. That's it. Boom. Instant marks in your pocket. The salutation is just as easy. You always, and I mean always, start with Dear Diary, followed by a comma. Don't try to get creative here. This is the way. All right, with the format locked in, let's move on to the most important part, the body. This is where you actually tell your story, and it's where your feelings are going to earn you the big marks. Now, you don't need to write a whole novel here. Just keep it short and focused. Two or three paragraphs is perfect. And in those paragraphs, you just need to do three things: describe what happened, express how you felt about it, and explain your reaction. And here it is, the most crucial point of all: you have to use emotional words, words like happy, sad, excited, nervous, proud. This is what separates a pretty good answer from a perfect, full-marks answer. So remember this: feelings equal full marks. Okay, enough talk. Let's actually put this all together. We're going to build a perfect, full-marks entry step-by-step, and you'll see just how simple this is.

He provides a step-by-step guide on how to write a diary entry for an English exam to achieve full marks. title: Dear Leese | Loneliness [Visual Diary Entry #1]
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I think that there is a loneliness epidemic. Loneliness is definitely something that's universal but not really talked about. And, it's interesting because a lot of people describe themselves as outcasts. But if everyone's an outcast, doesn't that mean that everyone is technically left out? So, it kind of made me think about my past, and it was really hard for me not to equate loneliness with being alone. I actually had a pretty tough time with making friends. Um, as social as I am and extroverted as I am, I felt like I was wasn't liked for who I was. And, that made me feel like no one wanted to be my friend, like no one enjoyed me genuinely, like me being myself. So, it made me shameful and embarrassed to be alone. So, in order to protect myself, I decided to reject them. I didn't want them to reject me. So, if they left me out, I would just block them entirely and kind of put myself in a position where it's like, "I'm going to be a loner by choice so then I don't have to get hurt by you." So, growing up, I used to be a competitive swimmer, so I used to swim two times a day, 2 hours in the morning, 3 hours at night. And, it was kind of insane, but it was pretty ironic that I didn't have a friend group or felt like I belonged in the swimming community, even though I say saw the same people like 5 hours a day. I think, eventually, I started to feel embarrassed about not having friends because I based my value as a person as how much I was able to make others happy. Because I was so scared of being rejected, I just kind of stayed on my own and thought that this would be best, um, just out of fear, I guess. I think I had a longing to belong somewhere. In high school, um, and even like a little bit of college, I never had a friend group

title: QUIET ORBIT | A Depression Anthem | Official Lyric Video
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I stop picking up the phone, stop explaining where I go. Every crowded room gets smaller till there's no more left to breathe. Too many voices hit at once, every sound becomes too much. I can feel my patience burning before I know what set it off. So I leave before I say something angry I didn't mean. I go quiet, close the distance, keep the damage far from reach. They call it cold from where they stand, but no one ever asks me why. Did you ever think I just disappear to stay in control? Did you ever ask what the noise was doing to my soul? I need a room where the world goes still, where nobody pulls at what I can't give. I need the space to come back down whenever every voice becomes too loud. Don't mistake my distance for goodbye, I still care from the other side. And if you've ever had to disappear just to feel your lungs again, I know why you choose the distance.

title: Diary Entry Writing for Class 7 | Full Explanation
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hello my dear students, aaj hamari English ki class mein rehne wali hai diary entry. Diary entry kya hoti hai? Diary entry hoti hai jo bhi aapke sath poore din mein vyateet ho chuka hai, usey aap ek diary mein likhein pratidin, aur ek format ke sath. Usey kehte hain diary entry. Toh aajiye aaj hum iska format samjhenge jo ki diary entry ko sahi tarike se likhne ka dhang hota hai aur isse aap exam mein full marks paa sakte hain. Aajiye format padhne ke liye. Date, Date jis din aap apni diary entry ko likh rahe hain, usi din ki yahan pe date daal denge. Uske baad day, aap isse milaan karke rakhiye, check karke rakhiye ki is din jo bhi date hai usi ka day hona chahiye. Time, jis samay aap likh rahe hain, woh time likhenge is par, jaise ki 9:00 baje abhi aur is par p.m. aur a.m. lagana mat bhoolna, jaise shaam ko likh rahe ho toh p.m. laga dena, subah likh rahe ho, subah ke samay mein toh a.m. laga dena. Uske baad aayega apna line space, line space aap exam sheet jo aapki rehne wali hai usme line space mat likhna L.S. karke, kyunki ispe aapke number cut sakte hain, teacher samjhega pata nahi kya bawal cheez likh di isne. Aap is jagah ek line chorr doge, maine aapko samjhane ke liye yahan pe L.S. likh diya hai aur line space, isliye aap ek line chorr dena single. Uske baad aap daaloge, Dear Diary, pyaari diary, aapki diary hai toh pyaari hi rehne wali hai. Uske baad aayegi hamari heading, heading jaisa aapka question rahega us hisab se aap apni heading daal denge isme. Phir aa jata hai hamara content, content bhi question ke hi... question se hi nikala jata hai content, jaisa ki aapko question diya gaya hai usi hisab se aap apna content likhenge. Content mein hamesha I ka use hota hai, woh ki aati hai first person mein, first person I ka use karoge aap hamesha content, kyunki aapki diary hai, aap khud likh rahe ho, kisi aur se toh likhvaoge nahi, khud likh rahe ho toh I ka use karoge diary mein toh I ka use karna hota hai. Uske baad aa jata hai, isme tense ka kaunsa use karna hai? Isme tense use hota hai past indefinite, aap poochoge ab ki past indefinite kyun hota hai? Past indefinite isliye hota hai kyunki aap jo diary mein likh rahe ho, woh pehle beet chuka hai, aapke sath woh ho chuka hai woh likhoge aap.

title: Unexpected Clarity  A Prison Memoir of Mental Liberation #journeeman #prisonlife #mindfulness
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
I've got something to say,
something that sticks in my throat like iron.
I miss my prison cell.
Not the wires, not the count, not the smell of bleach and sweat and locked metal.
I don't miss West Wing tier,
I don't miss Seg unit,
I don't miss cell 68.
I love my wife, my kids, my desk, the open sky when I step outside.
If you handed me the keys tomorrow and said 'Go back,' I'd burn them.
But listen,
there's a part of me that still walks those three meters by two and a half,
that still feels the quiet drop when the unit locks down.

Picture it.
Green door, heavy bolt,
grey vinyl-covered cabin wood,
tiny desk, bench that bites your spine, bed thinner than regret, toilet right there, no hiding.
Sink, small curtain with its ten-centimeter rule so they can always see you breathing.
Church guitar leaning against the wall like it's waiting for permission to sing, that's it.
That's the whole kingdom. And yet, when the day died and the televisions faded to mumbles, some footsteps echoed and then stopped, that box became still.
No notifications,
no opinions screaming from screens, 
no endless choices pretending to be freedom,
just me
and my mind.
They controlled everything else.

Time,
light,
movement,
who I spoke to,
when I ate,
when I pissed. Razor wire outside, laughing at the sky. But the mind, they couldn't touch it.
In that cage, my thoughts got room to stretch, to roam, to question everything I ever preached from a pulpit, to sit with doubt instead of burying it under sermons. Meditation wasn't an effort, it just happened like breathing,
like the fan humming, low light when the heat creeping through the pipe, a summer sweat turning the air to soup. I'd joke with the boys heading back to my chalet, make them laugh, 'it's a bloody cell, Malcolm.' Yeah, I'd say.
But tonight, it's my university.

category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: The final moments of David Wilcock are now coming into focus, and they paint a deeply troubling picture. According to reports from TMZ, Wilcock made a 911 call on Monday morning, just hours before his death. During that call, he spoke about serious financial problems and ongoing health issues. At one point, he told dispatch, quote, "I need to leave, I will be to the left of the house." Authorities say he refused to clarify whether he was armed or planning to harm himself. Dispatchers, meanwhile, treated the situation as urgent. In audio obtained by TMZ, officers can be heard describing the situation in real time, labeling it a potential suicide. Moments later, the situation escalated. As deputies arrived at his Colorado home, they approached with caution. The threat level was unclear, and backup was called in. Just before officers reached him, Wilcock said something else, quote, "I'm sorry to put you through this." And then, he hung up. Seconds later, deputies saw him outside the residence with a gun to his head. They took cover immediately, issuing commands to drop the weapon. But then, a single gunshot rang out. Authorities say Wilcock shot himself in front of responding deputies. No one else was found on the property after a search. He was pronounced dead at the scene. He was 53. Now, with details from that final call emerging, the tragedy surrounding David Wilcock is being seen in a new light, one shaped by personal struggles that remained largely hidden until the very end.

transcription: दोस्तों, परिस्थितियां सबके लिए एक जैसी नहीं होती और दूसरी बात यह कि प्रकृति से ज्यादा ताकतवर कुछ नहीं होता। यह बात असम के मामले में बिल्कुल सही साबित होती हुई दिखाई दे रही है। 12 से ज्यादा जिले प्रभावित हैं, 70 के आसपास मौतें हो चुकी हैं और 7 लाख से ज्यादा लोग उस असम में बाढ़ से परेशान हैं और अभी भी कई जानों की जाने का डर बना हुआ है और वहां के मुख्यमंत्री तक ने यह कह दिया है कि यह बड़ी चिंता की बात है। इतनी तेजी से बाढ़ पहले असम में नहीं आई थी। तो आखिर असम में इस तरह से बाढ़ अचानक से क्यों आ गई? तेजी से पानी कैसे भर गया? क्या मानसून जो कि बारिश का मौसम चल रहा है, इस वजह से हुआ है? तो क्या सिर्फ बाढ़ आने की जिम्मेदारी पूरी मानसून के ऊपर है या हमारा, आपका या हम जैसे कुछ लोगों का दोष है? चलिए सारी बातों को समझते हैं इस वीडियो में लेकिन सबसे पहले एक जरूरी जानकारी कि आपके लिए एक स्पेशल कोर्स आ चुका है IAS GS फाउंडेशन कोर्स। इस कोर्स की खास बात यह है कि अगर आप दिल्ली से या नोएडा से दृष्टि आईएएस की क्लास नहीं कर सकते और आप यही वाली क्लास ऑनलाइन करना चाहते हैं तो IAS GS फाउंडेशन लाइव ऑनलाइन कोर्स है। अब इस कोर्स की खास बात यह है कि 3 साल तक इस कोर्स की वैलिडिटी रहेगी। आप जितनी बार चाहें क्लास को उतनी बार देखिए। स्टडी मटेरियल हार्ड कॉपी में आपके घर पहुंचाया जाएगा तो आपको पढ़ने में भी मजा आएगा और इसके साथ ही आपको टेस्ट सीरीज प्रिलिम्स और मेंस की मिलेंगे और उसके साथ ही आंसर राइटिंग की प्रैक्टिस भी कराई जाएगी। इस वजह से यह आपके लिए बड़ा ही फायदेमंद है क्योंकि बेसिक से एडवांस तक सरल भाषा में आपको पूरा GS पढ़ाया जाएगा। आपको इसके बारे में अतिरिक्त जानकारी चाहिए तो वीडियो के डिस्क्रिप्शन में लिंक है, उसे क्लिक कर लीजिए या सीधे हमें कॉल कीजिए 87501 87501 पर। अब आते हैं हमारे टॉपिक पर। यहां पर सबसे पहली बात हम खबर को समझते हैं कि क्या है। देखिए, 66 से ज्यादा मौतें हो चुकी हैं, आंकड़े बढ़ते जा रहे हैं, 7 लाख लोग प्रभावित हैं, 856 गांव जो कि 12 जिलों के हैं वो प्रभावित हैं और 50,000 से ज्यादा लोग अभी राहत से वंचित हैं यानी कि वहां तक अभी भारत की सरकार या हम कहें असम की सरकार, सेना नहीं पहुंच पा रही है तो वह अभी इंतजार में हैं, ऐसे लोग भी हैं और इसके साथ ही असम राज्य आपदा प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण के अनुसार अभी और ज्यादा मुश्किल आने की इस डर बना हुआ है। अब अगली बात आती है कि ये सारी चीजें कैसे शुरू हुई? तो 19 जून को बाढ़ का पानी तेजी से खतरनाक स्तर पर पहुंचता है और जब वो खतरनाक स्तर पर पहुंचता है तो वो आसपास के इलाकों में बहना शुरू होता है और जिससे तीन सबसे ज्यादा शिवसागर, चराईदेव और जोरहाट, ये असम के ऐसे ऊपरी जिले हैं जहां पे सबसे पहले पानी बढ़ता है। क्यों? क्योंकि पानी ऊपर से ही नीचे आ रहा था तो जो ऊपर के जिले हैं वो प्रभावित होंगे और शिवसागर एक बहुत ही महत्वपूर्ण शहर है जो पानी के चपेट में यानी कि बाढ़ के चपेट में आया। कई लोग राहत शिविर में हैं, बहुत सारे काम चल रहे हैं लेकिन मैंने क्या कहा, इंसान प्रकृति के आगे एक छोटा सा खिलौना मात्र है, उससे ज्यादा कुछ नहीं।

transcription: गुड मॉर्निंग भाई लोगों! हाहाहा। तो किन-किन को लगता है कि मैं आप लोगों के कमेंट्स नहीं पढ़ता हूँ? अरे, कैसे नहीं पढ़ता हूँ भाई? रुको। अरे भाई मैं सबके कमेंट्स पढ़ता हूँ। हाँ, तुम पहले बोल लो। अरे मैं क्यों नहीं पढूंगा आप लोगों के कमेंट्स? अरे मैं सबके कमेंट्स पढ़ता हूँ गाइस। और अभी जो है, बहुत सारे कमेंट्स आ रहे हैं अलग-अलग वीडियोस के अंदर, अलग-अलग चीजों को लेकर। लेकिन एक कमेंट जो कि आप लोग सबसे ज्यादा कर रहे हैं, वो यह है कि सोनू भाई कहाँ हैं? सोनू भाई का क्या हुआ? तो भाई लोगों, एक बात बताऊं सच्ची-सच्ची? सोनू भाई है ना, उन ग्रेटेस्ट बंदों में से एक हैं जिन्हें मैं जानता हूँ या जिनसे मैं मिला हूँ। सोनू भाई सच में एक बहुत बहुत बहुत अच्छे इंसान हैं। और कमाल की बात पता है क्या? अब तो सोनू भाई ने भी अपना एक नया यूट्यूब चैनल बना लिया है गाइस! हाहाहा! मज़ा आ गया गाइस! तो सबसे पहले तो सोनू भाई को उनके नए चैनल के लिए हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं, बहुत बहुत बहुत सारी बधाइयां। और साथ ही साथ गाइस मैं तो आपसे भी यही कहूँगा कि जितना सपोर्ट और जितना प्यार आप लोगों ने आज तक हमारे लिए किया है ना, जितना प्यार हमें दिखाया है, गाइस उतना ही प्यार आप सोनू भाई के लिए भी दिखाइएगा, उतना ही सपोर्ट आप सोनू भाई को भी कीजिएगा। और साथ ही साथ गाइस मज़े की बात क्या है? सोनू भाई भी साइंस के बैकग्राउंड से आते हैं। तो आई होप कि सोनू भाई भी साइंस से रिलेटेड अच्छी-अच्छी वीडियोस आगे फ्यूचर के अंदर लेकर आएं, अच्छे-अच्छे एक्सपेरिमेंट्स करें। तो एक बार फिर से सोनू भाई को बहुत सारी बधाइयां। और गाइस आप लोग भी सोनू भाई को नीचे कमेंट्स के अंदर बहुत सारी बधाइयां जरूर देना, उनके चैनल पे जाकर भी, और ढेर सारा प्यार दिखाना। और गाइस एक बात बोलूं, एक और? देखो, अह मेरा मानना यह है कि हर इंसान को अपनी लाइफ के अंदर अपनी जर्नी, अपना रास्ता, अपनी मंज़िल चूज़ करने का पूरा-पूरा हक होता है। और ऐसा करना भी चाहिए। और जब आदमी है ना गाइस, अपने डिसीजन खुद से लेता है...

title: Steelers select Navy’s Eli Heidenreich in emotional 7th-round moment | 2026 NFL Draft
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: And Eli Heidenreich is here. You see the emotion hitting him. He is Navy's all-time receiver, all-time leading receiver. He was a zero star recruit coming out of high school. Valparaiso, Davidson, Slippery Rock offered him finally, his dream school. Grandfather was a naval officer, his uncle was a Navy corpsman and in the Marines. And Eli, now eligible with the new rules to defer his military service to pursue a career with the Steelers. I got goosebumps right now, Reese. I do. This, going into the draft, this timing is insane. This is my favorite player in the draft. Reese mentioned some of it, a running back, but only by position. The stats and positions right now compare nothing to what we're looking at here. Tears, the Naval uniform, the hat, the theater here in Pittsburgh going absolutely nuts. Hey, he had nearly, nearly 1,000 yards receiving in this Navy offense with stats. Well, Kyle mentioned it, that he had some Navy receiving records. This is my favorite stat of any prospect that we had in the draft. He had six receiving touchdowns in 2024. No player in the Naval Academy's history has ever had more than that. Just six, it's all it takes to make history. Six touchdowns in Navy is like 30 at LSU. Correct. God bless them. He's basically the Jamar Chase of Naval Academy wide receivers. But, what I love is his versatility. He's a runner, he obviously has great speed as well, the versatility here. He was good against good competition when they had those opportunities as well. One of the best players, no hyperbole, to come out of Navy in the last quarter century. What about against Air Force? The 8 catches 243 yards, those are records. Unbelievable, three touchdowns, but he was utilized in different ways they would line him up. Kyle, you watched him. I did. Dynamic. I grew up on the Severn River. The banks of the Severn River, Naval Academy, love the Naval Academy. Beautiful, right? That's right. Nice place, American life, Severn River. It's true. You see him back there, they go out to the slot, he catches it down field. And of all the places, Steelers, the hometown story. God bless these people in the Steelers draft. We're not only clapping, we're saluting. This is really cool, really cool. Really couldn't have scripted it any better too. We still had some picks to go, we still had things to do. But, you want to put an exclamation point on this draft in this city? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, I mean, look, this is one of the most iconic cities in, in, in the National Football League. It's just tradition rich. And you saw all the, you saw the, I mean, there was just genuine respect within the Pittsburgh Steelers draft room right there. It does give, gives me goosebumps. This is a great game, this is a great profession that we're involved in.

transcription: कन्या राशि की बात कर लेते हैं। आप लोग अजीब ही तरह के धर्म संकट में फंस गए हैं, क्योंकि जिन लोगों से आप मिल रहे हैं, आप उनके लिए अच्छा करना चाहते हैं, इनफैक्ट कोई आपका अगर दुश्मन भी है, आप उसके लिए भी अच्छा करना चाहते हो, आप सोचते हो कि चल तुझे भी नुकसान ना हो, लेकिन वो व्यक्ति इतना एडमेंट है अपना नुकसान कराने के लिए कि आप भी सोचते हैं कि यार क्या करूं? समझ नहीं आ रहा। है ना? तो बहुत कुछ सिखाने-समझाने की कोशिश करेंगे बट नथिंग इस गोइंग टू वर्क आउट। अगर आप लोग शादीशुदा हैं तो प्लीज जरा सावधान रहिएगा इस समय पे, क्योंकि ऐसा बहुत फ्रीक्वेंटली हो सकता है कि आप कोशिश तो बहुत करें कि चीजें सुधर जाएं, चीजें सही हो जाएं पर वो इवेंचुअली ना सुधरें और ना ही सही हों। नाउ बिकॉज़ ऑफ़ दिस, लाइफ कैन बी अ लिटिल टफ फॉर यू। आप लोग यू नो, हो सकता है कि आप सोचें कि चलो भाई, सामने वाले के लिए कुछ कर दिया जाए, सामने वाले को कुछ रास्ता दिखा दिया जाए, पर उसका व्यवहार आपके प्रति ऐसा हो कि, यू नो, नाउ यू थिंक लाइक ये तो किसी चीज के लायक ही नहीं है, इसके लिए कुछ करने की जरूरत नहीं है। तो, दिस कैन बी अ ह्यूज इश्यू फॉर यू। आपकी कुंडली के पहले घर में शुक्र यानी कि वीनस डेबिटिलेटेड रहेंगे, यानी नीच के रहेंगे, तो इसकी वजह से आप लोग इस महीने खुद पर ज्यादा ध्यान ना दें, अपने प्लेजर्स पर ज्यादा ध्यान ना दें, दूसरों के ऊपर बहुत ध्यान दें, ऐसा हो सकता है। नाउ, अगर आप ऐसी इंडस्ट्री में काम करते हैं जहां दूसरों के लिए आपको बहुत कुछ, यू नो, यू हैव टू डू फॉर देम, फिर तो समझ में आता है, जैसे अगर आप डॉक्टर हैं, आप फार्मासिस्ट हैं, आप लॉयर हैं, जहां पर आपको दूसरों के लिए ही कम्पलीटली अपना जीवन लगा देना है, देन इन दैट पोजीशन थिंग्स डोंट सीम बैड, आपको बहुत ज्यादा काम करने को मिलेगा, आपको बहुत हार्ड तोड़ मेहनत करनी पड़ेगी, दैट विल बी, यू नो, अ वेरी डिफिकल्ट थिंग टू डू। तो, आपको अपने लिए बहुत ज्यादा टाइम नहीं मिलेगा, इनफैक्ट अगर आप सोने की भी सोच रहे होंगे तो नींद में भी आपका काम आपके दिमाग में चल रहा होगा। सो, दैट कैन डेफिनेटली बी एन इश्यू हियर, जिसकी वजह से आप लोग ढंग से सोए नहीं, ढंग से अपने ऊपर ध्यान ना दें। सेहत को लेकर एंजायटी आप लोगों के मन में ज्यादा हो सकती है, एक तो सोओगे नहीं, ऊपर से ऑब्वियसली जब सोते नहीं हैं तो ग्रॉगी सा फील होता है, खराब सा फील होता है, तो आपको लगेगा कि अरे यार, कुछ मुझे हो तो नहीं गया? कोई प्रॉब्लम तो नहीं है? तो ऐसी सेहत को लेकर एंजायटी आप लोगों के अंदर जरूर देखने को मिल सकती है, उसका आप लोग ध्यान दीजिएगा। डोंट अलाउ इट टू रन योर लाइफ। हालांकि, अगर हम ओवरऑल देखें, तो आप लोग कार्यक्षेत्र में अच्छा कर सकते हैं, ऐसी कोई बहुत बड़ी प्रॉब्लम नहीं है। आप लोग अपना बेस्ट देने की कोशिश करेंगे और जिन भी लोगों के साथ आप काम करते हैं, उनको ये डिफरेंस जरूर महसूस हो जाएगा, दैट यू आर पुटिंग इन मोर देन योर 100% और उसके लिए आपको सर्टेनली अवार्ड्स, रिवार्ड्स जो भी हैं, वो भी जरूर मिल जाएंगे, तो परेशान होने की जरूरत नहीं है। कई बार आपका जो इंट्यूशन है, वो बिल्कुल टॉप क्लास रहेगा, आपको एग्जैक्टली पता रहेगा कि कहां पर क्या करना है और आपके जो सीनियर्स हैं, जूनियर्स हैं, जिनके साथ भी आप काम करते हो, वो इसको जरूर एप्रिशिएट करेंगे।

title: Alysa Liu reacts to winning gold after free skate
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: A script that would have been rejected as far-fetched and a comeback that has brought her all the way perhaps to the Olympic podium. It is like she's just playing on the ice, not even performing anymore. The joy, the passion, and she's figured out how to compete without carrying the weight of it. She stays so loose and completely herself out there. That's the secret every athlete wants to solve. That's what I'm talking about. I can't believe it. Thank you so much. Amazing. Amazing. Those are her right? I can't even believe this. The toe was amazing, the Lutz was amazing. Guys, I don't know if you believe what you've been watching since she made her comeback. But, but through it all, she's just kind of been like, "Oh, this is fun." I've never seen a comeback like it, and I've never seen someone withstand pressure like Alyssa Liu. And she did tell us that it's a whole new world this time around because she doesn't feel like her life is on the line. She has like this nonchalance both to the way she jumps and performs. Triple Lutz, triple toe, very nice second element in the program, and it just got better from there. She is just all sunshine on the ice. If you don't watch her skate and want to get on the ice and just feel what it might feel like to race around the rink, it is childlike, beautiful joy and innocence out there. Quad God loved it. So did everybody else in this arena, including her dad, her siblings, and Alyssa as well. She really couldn't have done better. This has been incredible to watch, 2 and a half years away from competition, Lori.

title: “I Was Genuinely Freaked Out” Curry Barker, Inde Navarrette & Michael Johnston on ‘Obsession’
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hi, I'm Indiana Massara. And I'm Michael Johnston. And I'm writer-director Kirby Barker. Today we're interviewing each other for our new film, Obsession. I love you so, so, so, so, so, so much. A love only the branch of a willow tree could conjure. What was your reaction when you first read the script and how did you feel watching Obsession with a big crowd at TIFF? I got my hands on the script and I said, "What can I do to be a part of it?" title: What Reading My Old Journal Taught Me About Growth
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I read my journal from a year ago and cried, in a good way. So, I did something kind of embarrassing last week. I went back and read my journal from a year ago and I cried, and I want to tell you why that was actually a good thing. The journal was from about 12 months ago. I'd completely forgotten I even had entries from that period. It was one of those stretches that just kind of blurred by. Nothing dramatic, nothing memorable, just a lot of Tuesdays. But I picked it up on a slow Sunday and started from the beginning. And here's the strange part. I didn't recognize the person writing it, not because they were sad or doing badly, but because I had completely forgotten what that version of me was worried about, what they were hoping for, what felt impossible, and what felt small. And reading it felt like getting a letter from someone I used to know. Some of it was small. I'd written about a coffee that was really good, about being annoyed at someone in a way I couldn't even reconstruct now, about a plan I had that I was nervous about, and looking back, I know it worked out fine, but the version of me writing it didn't know that yet. And that's the thing that hit me. The person writing that entry was doing something really hard without knowing it. They were living through uncertainty with no knowledge of the outcome, and they showed up and wrote it down anyway. That's not a small thing. I don't think I would have remembered any of it if I hadn't written it. Not because it wasn't worth remembering, but because our brains aren't built for this. They compress time, they flatten the details, they remember the outcome and forget the journey. Here's the one that really got me. There was an entry about something I was trying to get better at, I won't go into detail, but it was something I'd been struggling with for a while. At the time of writing, it felt like I wasn't making any progress. But reading it a year later, I knew I had, not dramatically, not in a montage moment
